From: **Rev. Raphael Warnock**
Subject: Your thoughts on RFK Jr. and Pete Hegseth
| | |
---
Friend – something’s been on my mind, and I need to know where you stand on it.
Donald Trump and his allies claim they’re championing “meritocracy.” But that’s absurd.
You can’t lecture me about “merit” and then make Pete Hegseth your Secretary of Defense.
You can’t lecture me about “merit” and then make Robert F. Kennedy Jr. your Secretary of Health and Human Services.
You can’t preach about promoting a “meritocracy” while filling your Cabinet with the most unfit, unqualified people ever selected.
**Let’s be clear: I’m doing everything I can to hold the line against this dangerous administration, and I need to know if you’re as concerned as I am about the threats Trump’s Cabinet poses to our country. Please, let me know now:**
**Do you approve of Trump’s Cabinet?**
| | | [YES](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123270283/594906118/-1591861468?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&code=jtk5692-su-nd2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTEvMS85MDkwMSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMjA0ZWNmNS1kYmYwLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=k2AeDIqxEI8wtYrbdcZdIdJ2bKpMoedo-QN1AT6OQJo=&emci=977ef4d6-0ff0-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=f204ecf5-dbf0-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=1586379)

Friend, I want America to win – because I love this country.
I love it in the same way we love our families. Many families have a complicated story. I carry in my veins the brutal side of that. My daddy had to give up his bus seat while wearing his soldier’s uniform – but because we kept fighting for America, his son now sits in a _Senate_ seat.
No matter what Trump and his allies throw at us, I’ll never give up on the fight to make this country a better place. I’m grateful to know you’re with me in this fight.
Thanks for speaking out,
Rev. Raphael Warnock

Trump just left the stage here in Michigan and is boarding a plane back to
Washington.

Before taking off, he praised my extreme GOP opponent, Mike Rogers — and
then spouted a conspiracy theory that the 2024 election was rigged against
Rogers.

There is no doubt that Donald Trump is going ALL IN on flipping Michigan.
He already endorsed Mike Rogers, effectively clearing the GOP field. Then,

back him. Now, Trump has made Michigan his FIRST battleground visit of

| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn't a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal -- the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God's grace. **

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." **_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.

In the months since Charlie's assassination, there has been a massive surge of interest in Turning Point USA's message among young Americans...

...and it's not just the conservative message as a whole -- _**it 's the message of FAITH! **_

In recent months, I have heard countless stories of people who have answered Charlie's call to attend a Bible study, start a family, and pray to God.

Charlie devoted so much of his time urging people to build strong families, to go to church, and to stand up for America. _And it 's happening. _

After years of witnessing declining church attendance, we are now seeing Americans filling the pews in huge numbers across the country.

What we're witnessing is not just growth --**it 's revival. **

At Turning Point USA, we are dedicated and honored to continue strengthening the faith of Americans, young and old.

We are building a coalition of truth-preaching churches that stand firm against cultural compromise, defend biblical values, and strengthen families.

We are training pastors, uniting congregations, and, of course, reaching the next generation on campuses across the country with this same message.

You might feel disheartened by the evil in our culture and by the unthinkable assassination of Charlie.

**But America 's faithful are waking up. The youth are waking up. America is waking up. **

All across this nation, pastors are linking arms, young believers are finding their voice, and families are saying, _" We're not backing down." _

This is what Charlie prayed for.

I see this book as one of Charlie's most enduring gifts to the world, and I know you will too.

None of us knew how brief his time on earth would be. But the truths written in this book are timeless. They will outlive us all, and most importantly, **_so will the legacy of Charlie 's faith. _**

Charlie lived life at a relentless pace, but he also understood the sacred value of stillness. Through it all, his gaze was fixed on eternity with God.

No one should face financial ruin for wanting an education or getting the healthcare they need. People pursuing higher education and seeking healthcare are doing what they’re supposed to do, and they shouldn’t be punished for it.
In fact, healthcare and education are human rights, and they should be accessible for everyone.
With the racial wealth gap continuing to widen, cancelling debt is also a racial justice issue, along with economic and gender justice.
Plus it’s incredibly popular with the American people; polls show that 84% of _Republican voters_ want to cancel medical debt.
We already have great policies on this:
I co-led 2024’s** _Medical Debt Cancellation Act_** , which would eliminate all $220 billion in medical debt held by millions of Americans, wipe it from credit reports, and drastically limit the accrual of future medical debt.
I’ve also co-sponsored legislation such as the **_Medicare for All Act_** _,_ the __**_Student Debt Cancellation Act_** , and the **_College for All Act_** , which would make community colleges free and eliminate tuition and fees for most families at public four-year colleges.

Today, _The Economist_ and YouGov released a poll finding, for the first time, that more Americans want to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) than don't.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8afe3877-c68b-42e5-95a0-6758fa214ce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
According to the [poll](https://substack.com/redirect/d9dd22de-30bb-4edc-89f2-5d9f2f868ea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), 46 percent of people support getting rid of ICE, compared to 43 percent who oppose its abolition. This represents a major shift in public opinion--this same polling outfit found only 27 percent support for abolishing ICE as recently as July. Today's survey also found that most Americans believe ICE is making them less, not more safe, by a margin of 47 percent to 34 percent.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5d0aaf6e-9a5d-41f7-bc86-dda0b8b54a75?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In perfect form, this morning the centrist advocacy group Third Way released a [memo](https://substack.com/redirect/18bdcebe-036c-4ece-827d-c440c78194ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) warning Democrats not to call for dismantling ICE, arguing that "politically, it is lethal." Their evidence includes a focus group they conducted in October, which...is dumb. ICE's execution of Renee Nicole Good has broken through--_[69 percent](https://substack.com/redirect/d9dd22de-30bb-4edc-89f2-5d9f2f868ea5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ of Americans report having seen video of the shooting. This has clearly impacted public opinion in a way that makes information from months ago significantly irrelevant.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a6fd379-fad7-499c-a627-32c1d659f0c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We cannot let the Third Ways of the world--the centrist establishment muckety mucks whose version of the Democratic Party already lost to Trump, twice--win this debate. It's simply too important.
There are lots of reasons to dismantle ICE. There's a functional argument: We do not need ICE to enforce immigration laws; the U.S. handled this just fine for 227 years prior to the creation of this specific agency. There's a fiscal argument: ICE is now larger than every other federal law enforcement agency _combined_. It's larger than the [militaries](https://substack.com/redirect/bf7d7258-6a33-4403-a754-4b5be07233ff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of all but 15 countries in the world! It's annual budget, $37.5 billion, could [pay](https://substack.com/redirect/9933a788-82b1-4ba0-8386-d207409bae63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the health insurance of every needy child in the country!
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE4NDQ3OTY1MCwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc2ODM1MDAxNiwiZXhwIjoyMDgzOTI2MDE2LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.wfMKojwtfb0CTTd2lHa0O1MovBUK5AHWQKsKp4-V4aQ?)
But the core reason for abolishing ICE is that it poses a structural threat to American democracy. This is an unaccountable agency, _by design_. ICE is not subject to the rules governing local or state police departments; there are no laws barring ICE agents from wearing masks, driving in unmarked cars, and operating in plainclothes. ICE was designed after 9/11 to support the FBI's domestic terrorism efforts, with almost nothing in the way of transparency or guardrails. So what happens when domestic terrorism gets defined as expressing "opposition to law and immigration enforcement; extreme views in favor of mass migration and open borders; adherence to radical gender ideology, anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, or anti-Christianity," and "hostility towards traditional views on family, religion, and morality," as Trump's [NSPM-7](https://substack.com/redirect/eca7c400-9c50-43cb-96c7-615e1de29e6a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) directive and Attorney General Pam Bondi's recent [memo](https://substack.com/redirect/bd4a2422-c265-4937-b701-c6c8ed641caf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the FBI do?
Well, what happens is everything that we are seeing from ICE today--a federal agency operating quite explicitly as Trump's personal militia. Mussolini had his Blackshirts, Hitler had his SS, and Trump has ICE--an army of ideologically motivated MAGA loyalist chuds whose new members owe their employment not to the state (being largely unqualified for positions in legitimate law enforcement agencies) but rather to Trump's personal patronage.
The existence of this profoundly unaccountable, overtly fascist military apparatus poses a _structural_ danger to our democracy. Structural dangers like this can't be reformed--they need to be dismantled. "We shouldn't have a Gestapo in this country" isn't a radical position. It's actually the only non-radical position you can take on the question. That's long been true morally. And today's polling shows it's true politically, as well. In every way, abolishing ICE is now the moderate position.
So email your Democratic elected officials, call their offices, speak up at their town halls. Tell our Democratic representatives and senators that they need to use every tool at their disposal--including, in the near term, the [Congressional appropriations process](https://substack.com/redirect/c7353ab7-408d-4bab-99f0-603b743fc2eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--to stand up to this rogue militia. And help our Democratic leaders understand--if we are so lucky, come 2028, to get a second chance at resetting our democracy--that getting rid of Trump's SS is nonnegotiable.
Thanks for reading--and if you want more folks to see this message, please feel free to share!

subject: This work transcends any age group
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
This is the coalition that could change everything.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260113-1&t=1&akid=3044%2E587540%2EQQtpWk)
Peter,
There’s a new kind of Democratic coalition forming — one that could transform politics as we know it.
It’s made up of people who’ve lived through the consequences of a government that failed them, from Boomers who protested Vietnam and are now back in the streets demanding no Kings in America and volunteering on many of the campaigns we are supporting, to Gen Z voters and candidates rising up to lead this country forward.
We may come from different generations, but we’re united by one truth: We’re done waiting for someone else to fix this.
And that’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve is about. We’re building a political home for everyone who believes it’s time to put a new generation of progressives in power.
**[Will you pitch in $5 now to help us elect young progressive leaders?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260113_1_intergenerational.0ULI2q&refcode=em20260113-3044&amount=5&t=2&akid=3044%2E587540%2EQQtpWk)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260113_1_intergenerational.0ULI2q&amount=5&refcode=em20260113-3044&t=21&akid=3044%2E587540%2EQQtpWk)**
Some of the strongest supporters of this movement are folks decades older than the candidates we’re backing, and I think that’s powerful as hell. It shows that the narrative about this being about old vs. young isn’t true. It's about status quo vs a new way of doing things, something people of all ages can get behind. It proves that this whole movement we’re building isn’t just about age. It’s about urgency and shared purpose.
We don’t need less of the older generation, we need all hands on deck. Because when a third of the country is Gen Z or Millennial but we barely have a fraction of the power, we are failing to deliver the government that all Americans deserve.
We’ve seen what happens when we come together across generations. We’ve watched it block abortion bans. We’ve watched it win statehouse races. And we’re just getting started.
If we can grow this Boomer Zoomer coalition, or whatever we end up calling it (feel free to send us your name suggestions!), we can build a Democratic Party strong enough to put a check on Trump and finally start rebuilding this country.
That work starts right now. With you.
**[Peter, if you’re with us, make a $5 contribution to power our work.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260113_1_intergenerational.0ULI2q&refcode=em20260113-3044&amount=5&t=22&akid=3044%2E587540%2EQQtpWk)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

clean_body: It would mean the world to us if you read this | | | | | | | | Dear Patriot , This is Brigadier General James Emory Mace, U.S. Army (Retired), and my wife, Anne. As parents, there's nothing harder than watching your child fight a battle you can't fight for them. But because of you--because of your support --our daughter can keep going. Let us explain. We remember the night she told us. Her hands were shaking. She thought she'd disappointed everyone she loved. But we raised her to believe that setbacks don't define you--how you rise does. With a WWII veteran for a father and a schoolteacher for a mother, she grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again: 👉 Never quit. 👉 Never run from the truth. 👉 And never let anyone tell you that you areless than what God made you to be. So we gave her a choice: Go back to school ... or get a job. Most kids in that situation fall apart. But not Nancy. She picked herself up, took a job at Waffle House, and fought her way back. Soon after, she was elected as the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. House of Representatives. She 's been fighting her whole life; for herself, for her kids, for the truth, and now... for her state. As parents, we've been blessed to see the overwhelming support she's received from patriots across the nation. But each day that goes out there and fights for you, she 's up against the knife. The Establishment has its pitchforks aimed at our daughter. They stalk her. Send her death threats. She 's even been physically assaulted. As parents, we won't lie--it's hard sitting back and watching our daughter face relentless attacks day after day. But Nancy is our daughter. And we know this: She never backs down. And she never stops fighting. So today, we have just one ask: Patriot , if Nancy's going to pull this off and save our beloved state of South Carolina, she needs your backup. Please, from two parents who love their daughter with everything they have ... Help us fight the battle against the Radical Left with her. May God bless you and your family. 🙏 With respect, General James Emory Mace (Ret.) and Anne Mace Proud Parents of Nancy Mace | | | | | | |

Donald Trump promised to stack the courts with “his judges.” And he’s
delivered — with results that are nothing short of disastrous.

Trump’s judges are partisan hacks. Since taking the bench, they have voted
in Trump’s favor 133 times and opposed him only 12.

That’s a staggering 92% alignment with one man, not the law.

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/55459?c0=dj-em-20260113.gAPjn8&refcode=em20260113-61078&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=61078%2E1407376%2EEL8fCU ]Tweet from Demand Justice: Trump's judges aren't impartial, they're his
cronies. Trump's appellate judges have ruled in his favor 133 times out of
145 cases - that's what a rigged system looks like.

And the consequences are jaw-droppingly bad. These judges have:

* Greenlit Trump to deploy the National Guard, ignoring the protests of
governors and mayors who actually know what they’re doing.
* Dragged their feet on investigating why flights carrying Venezuelan
immigrants to a foreign prison ignored a court order — because in
their minds, obeying the law is optional.
* Rubber-stamped withholding millions from public schools, leaving kids
and teachers to pay the price while showing loyalty to Trump instead
of the Constitution.

...that’s just the tip of the iceberg.

Make no mistake: these judges are only siding with Trump to curry favor,
angle for a future Supreme Court seat, and turn our courts into a
political loyalty test.

Demand Justice is taking a stand against this full-scale attack on
judicial independence. Because if we don’t act now, Trump’s judges will
shape decisions for decades to come.

Fellow Conservative,

Over the weekend, I began seeing photographs coming out of Iran of young women lighting cigarettes from the flames created by burning photos of the Iranian Ayatollah.

What a brave, bold act of defiance against a tyrannical, murderous government who terrorizes its own people and chants “Death to America.”

**Iranians want freedom.**

Iranians want fundamental human rights, and they are protesting by the thousands to defy the regime that has spent decades murdering Iranians and murdering Americans as the world’s largest state sponsor of terror.

https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/- We’re running out of time, Peter. Hundreds of people from around the country have stepped up today for Giving Tuesday, but we’re still running short of the 1,000 members we need to unlock an additional $100,000 for our work before midnight tonight. And with the Trump administration accelerating some of the most extreme anti-environment, pro-polluter attacks in modern history,falling short is simply not an option. We’re asking you, Peter: will you renew your LCV membership right now while membership is only $5 to help us unlock an additional $100,000 to oppose the Trump administration’s attempts to exploit our public lands and roll back climate progress? https://links.messages.lcv. This isn’t just about hitting a number. It’s about having the resources we need to challenge these increasingly reckless orders and attempts to shred environmental safeguards — and stop the polluter handouts that Trump and his allies are fast-tracking. RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/Pwb7C7A-_ Every single person who steps up today is critical to our efforts — here’s why this Giving Tuesday is so important: Trump is trying to erase the scientific and legal foundation of climate action. By dismantling the Endangerment Finding, which affirms that greenhouse gas emissions harm our health and welfare, Trump’s EPA would hand fossil fuel companies a free pass to spew climate pollution into our air. He’s also ending the program that required big polluters to report their pollution, making it nearly impossible to track what they’re spewing or hold them accountable.
Decades of established pollution protections are being peeled away. More than a dozen rules that keep toxic pollution out of the air we breathe and water we drink to protect our health are on the chopping block, tossed aside to allow fossil fueled power plants to cut corners and shift the burden of their damage onto our communities.
The Trump administration is giving away the Arctic to corporate polluters, working to allow more drilling in one of the planet’s last intact ecosystems. Mining roads carved through national parks and preserves. Fire-sale auctions in critical ecosystems. Hundreds of millions of acres of U.S. waters off Alaska potentially opened to drilling. It could do irreparable damage to wildlife, our climate, and Alaska Native communities. We’re working every day with our 30 state affiliates, organizing on the ground, exposing backroom deals and corruption, rallying voters, and defending the treasured and unique places that define our country. But meeting this moment requires resources — especially as we go up against big polluters and fossil fuel opponents. This $100,000 match challenge, and how many people step up this Giving Tuesday, will determine how hard we can push back. Peter, your renewal right now powers our work to protect people and the planet. Will you renew before MIDNIGHT TONIGHT to help keep this movement strong when it matters most? $5 is all it takes. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/7RYwsX9~ Every contribution brings us closer. And the clock is ticking. Thanks for standing with us, Chris Brooks

Team: Changes at the U.S. Postal Service are going to make a known problem even worse, and it could affect thousands of voters across the country in this November’s midterm elections.
Legally speaking, the date stamped on your mail is when it counts as being sent, from your bills to your taxes to your ballot. For decades, that's been stamped the day you gave it to the United States Postal Service (USPS), whether you handed it to your mail carrier, left it in a mailbox, or dropped it at the local post office.
That's no longer the case. Your mail will be stamped the day it hits a regional processing facility , not your local post office. That could be a day, or more, later than when you handed your mail over, thanks to the Trump administration's "cost-cutting" efforts.
How does this impact vote-by-mail? If you live in a state with a mail-in ballot grace period -- something most states still have, even though MAGA is trying to end those -- your ballot still counts if it was postmarked by Election Day and received in the grace period after Election Day. In this case, however, a ballot mailed on Election Day may not be postmarked as Election Day, making your ballot automatically invalid even though you followed the rule of law and the postmark date is out of your control.
We have to make sure every voter understands this change and how it can impact them -- from vote-by-mail, to their bills, their taxes, legal replies to companies, everything. What Americans think is the mailing deadline may not be the deadline anymore and that's a huge deal that's being under-reported by the media.

subject: Judicial Watch Urges Supreme Court to Keep Fifth Circuit Ban on Counting Ballots Received After Election Day
body:
“Counting ballots received after Election Day is a flagrant violation of federal law and encourages fraud and voter distrust,” said Judicial Watch President Tom Fitton. “Let us hope that the Supreme Court will decline to hear Mississippi’s senseless attempt to overturn a historic decision that sensibly concluded that counting ballots received after Election Day is unlawful.”

A federal judge in Washington state on Friday blocked the Trump administration from enforcing key parts of an executive order that sought to change how states administer federal elections. Washington Democrats and their radical left New York City allies just launched a redistricting lawsuit aimed at one thing, flipping Staten Island and Brooklyn’s congressional seat without earning a single vote. | Friends, Let’s be very clear about what’s happening. | Washington Democrats and their radical left New York City allies just launched a redistricting lawsuit aimed at one thing, flipping Staten Island and Brooklyn’s congressional seat without earning a single vote. | | Their solution is as absurd as it is insulting. They want to jam Staten Island and Manhattan into the same congressional district, pretending communities with nothing in common should share representation. That is not representation. That is manipulation. This lawsuit has nothing to do with fairness. It is a blatant attempt to silence Staten Island voters and hand Democrats another seat so they can push higher taxes, weaker public safety, and the same failed policies New Yorkers are fleeing. I am the ONLY Republican member of Congress from New York City. I flipped this seat because voters were fed up. Democrats know they lose when voters have a real choice, so they are trying to redraw the map instead of respecting the people. Defending our district is not cheap. It is not quick. The first major election of the year isn't getting enough attention from the media or Democrats.
On April 7th of this year, MAGA is desperately hoping to win a rubber match in the upcoming Wisconsin state Supreme Court race.
---

This is a must-win for MAGA. After last year's massive win for Democrats, they now hold a 4-3 majority on the WI court. With a seat up for grabs this year, Democrats now have a chance to expand their majority to 5-2.
And more importantly, a win this April would lock down the court for Democrats until at least 2030, securing a key swing state court for the rest of Trump's presidency.
In 2025, Trump and MAGA attempted coups at the state level in Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. If they had seized control of those state Supreme Courts, they would have gained control over the body that has final say on election laws/results, allowing them to rig elections in these crucial states in their favor in 2026 and 2028.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yPkw48F4m1zL3EMpBTQOYj0znT_QLhQgNFoI4lPwqFiNrJ2HMVWSGHskyUricM8ur7oXa2EWoxZ1ZCugrKv5BD9BjFkI4gc7l9NWDLLfFWIMxekQdb46fH6zf7kOhClg4E4lcoAQGGJVLpeH2xER6gbAoDbefHlZhl7ZYr2HagwHMHnAHbp1UW0KqBksOQC8XS9iTSYTI3pjlR2omhHvAysqH3J7MZ3EIt-MFA-zHC5oxS9HQV_MDw==&c=NIA-MsoB3iarjkOxnZiJ_iQj3CIzzGUyq2pi8bHXi8zHlNEogJfB5w==&ch=inFE-K3dGGhdV8vXOZJADJaSJdofHqVWr0USfz4FKdsO4Scyt0jvbQ==)
---
The stakes in the PA Supreme Court race were existential for Democrats' 2028 hopes. But we rallied and won a decisive victory. We need the same energy in the upcoming WI race.
---

In PA, Defend Our Courts helped lead the defense of the liberal majority on the court. Despite millions of dollars spent by MAGA to try and take the court, Pennsylvanians turned out in record numbers and handed Democrats a 30+ point blowout victory.
In Philadelphia, where we concentrated much of our voter outreach along with digital and TV ads, turnout surged by 34%. That was the largest increase in the state.
We defended the PA court and kept the Democrats' 2028 chances alive. Now we're going on the offensive in Wisconsin to secure Dems' path back to the White House.

| Police Officers Association of Michigan Endorses Doug Lloyd for Attorney General
Pre-Convention endorsement underscores that prosecutorial experience wins statewide elections
LANSING, MI - Doug Lloyd, candidate for Michigan Attorney General, today announced the endorsement of the Police Officers Association of Michigan (POAM), a leading organization representing law enforcement professionals across the state.
The endorsement comes ahead of the Republican endorsement convention and highlights the strength of Lloyd's prosecutorial background in a race that will ultimately be decided by voters statewide. POAM represents law enforcement employees throughout Michigan and advocates for public safety, economic security, and strong support for those who protect Michigan communities.
"As a prosecutor, I've worked side by side with law enforcement to hold violent offenders accountable and keep communities safe," said Doug Lloyd. "This endorsement shows that experience matters and that prosecutors with a record of enforcing the law can win in a general election. Michigan needs an Attorney General who understands the job from day one."
[Lloyd has already earned the endorsement of more than 60 county prosecutors, over 30 sheriffs, and dozens of retired judges, prosecutors, and sheriffs, as well as the current and former Michigan House Judiciary Committee Chairs. ](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001HC3JUciKWA7yCOC7ifVkUVYjYkL0ayebOhYVhQETlmev06fCnuJ8d34v4x_R8gpz0F6-Q7hKJpICIxS_I6egi2pXnBW43FHoNR2cSCyT1z4nakfxQep9IFFeM-VCqDttzwarpAHjjbD_g3WxAI9lIWUH6Qb4ZL0LrGh8mSyknsm8F5f-w6e6_A==&c=dlaXaA3EUJ4z254HwPdtQUMI3pFYs-4IH_WV6aKZIgc5JMH7Q5-RHw==&ch=nc9CiApK1Ial_vGTHOJTw9voKSf0KQ2L8rJIuDHTiLSUtqkLuhoozQ==)Together, those endorsements reflect broad confidence from leaders who have firsthand experience enforcing and shaping Michigan law.
Lloyd has made restoring law and order, supporting victims, and standing with law enforcement central to his campaign. The POAM endorsement further reinforces his record, readiness, and ability to win statewide.

I came across a post the other day involving Vivek Ramaswamy, and it was one of those moments where you can see the whole machine working in real time.
Here's the setup. Vivek does an interview from his house. He's dressed the way you would expect for a serious interview, suit, tie, hair done. The kind of shot that is almost always framed waist-up. But then a wider angle photo circulates online showing he's not wearing shoes.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c4e34a6c-1ad6-44df-83bc-769acfb742fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
And immediately, the comments go where you already know they will go.
Not policy. Not competence. Not the direction of the state. It turns into cultural pile-on. Indian. Not "really" American. Religion. Heritage. The usual xenophobic sludge.
Now I want to be careful here, because I do not live in the "everyone is racist" universe. I am not interested in the identity-politics dopamine hit where every disagreement gets flattened into a label.
I am half Nigerian. I have seen racism. The blunt kind. The ugly kind. And I will also tell you this. The overwhelming majority of people I have known in my life are good people that don't give a shit about race. 9,999 out of 10,000 are good people. Most people are not sitting around trying to hate their neighbors.
But this was not subtle. This was not policy critique. This was a moment where you could watch a joke turn into a narrative, and then watch that narrative mutate into something uglier because it benefits politically.
That's the point of this section.
### The Question for Amy Acton and Democrats
So I'm asking Democrats, and I'm asking Amy Acton's campaign directly. Is it a moral win if you win because your opponent is being dragged through a racial and xenophobic narrative that your own party claims to oppose?
If your brand and party is inclusion, equity, diversity, anti-discrimination, and "silence is violence," what exactly do you do when the ugliness is pointed at your opponent and not you?
Do you speak up because it is right, even if it costs you?
Or do you sit with consultants and say nothing because it helps you at the polls? Let them "eat their own" as the saying goes.
And if you do nothing, what does that make you? Are you the person that says we need to be antiracist then benefits from racism?
I am not asking this as a rhetorical dunk. I am asking because this is exactly where politics is right now. It is WWE. It is content. It is angle shooting. It is letting the worst instincts in the room run wild because it is strategically convenient.
The Democratic Party cannot spend a decade preaching moral superiority and then magically go quiet when the moral test shows up in their own race.
### The Internet Is Not Organic Anymore
I also want to say something that people keep pretending is not true.
A lot of this online discourse is not real in the way people assume it is real. It is psyops. It is agenda-driven. It is bait. It is engagement farms and bots and coordinated narrative shaping that starts as an initial spark and then spreads because real humans pick it up and repeat it.
I keep thinking about how even smart people get sucked into it. Charles Hoskinson, the creator of Cardano, got lured into arguing with a bot earlier this year. Not because he is dumb, but because the bot was designed to trigger him.
That is where we are. The internet can manufacture a "controversy," then manufacture the talking points around it, then wait for human beings to make it mainstream by repeating it.
So when I see the Vivek no-shoes photo turn into "he is not American," I do not even know how much of it is real people versus the bots, the parties, foreign actors.
But I do know this. If you benefit from it and stay silent, the hypocrisy is apparent.
### The Double Standard
And this is where the entire thing becomes absurd.
If you have ever done an interview from home, you already know how this works. You dress for the camera frame. You do not dress for the part of your body that the audience will never see.
I ran for Congress. I did interviews in my house. No shoes. And I'll be damned if you are walking into my house with shoes on. That is not happening.
The irony here is that the "gotcha" is not even a gotcha. It's just a photo that was never intended for broadcast. Even if it was it was behind the scenes.
And once people start doing "culture" attacks, it reminds me of all those old internet moments where people mock other communities for eating with their hands, and then the internet takes five minutes to remind everyone that Americans eat with their hands constantly. Remember when this happened to Mamdani?
[](https://substack.com/redirect/e784d293-2b65-4fa4-b94c-07fc37ec14a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We eat French fries. KFC. Hamburgers. Pizza. Chips. Ribs. Wings. Shit, they give us a damn bib to eat ribs & wings. But eating rice with your hands for some reason is insane and un-American?
The mockery is not about the act. It's about who is doing it.
That's what's happening here.
### John McCain Showed What Moral Courage Looks Like
[](https://substack.com/redirect/9002c085-d569-4670-9dc5-9fa69c63c697?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This whole thing also brings me back to one of the few political moments from the modern era that still holds up.
John McCain, during that town hall, defended Barack Obama. A supporter tries to paint Obama as something dangerous. And McCain shuts it down. He says he knows Obama, and that he's a good man, a family man.
McCain probably lost votes that day. He did it anyway.
And **that 's** the reason we still talk about that clip today. Not because it changed the election outcome, but because it revealed character. It revealed a boundary. It proved there was a line he would not cross even if it helped him.
We do not talk about that moment because it was strategic.
We talk about it because it was the right things to do.
### The Choice in Front of Amy Acton Is Simple
So here's what I think the solution is...

**[It's RMD Time Again.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e1111645/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsejFCdFd5WA/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWd8iA/sbue2c1e900)** **Imagine opening your retirement statement this year...** And realizing that a simple decision - one most retirees never even think about - could reshape your taxes, your diversification, and even your long-term financial stability. Every year, Americans over age 73 are forced to withdraw **tens of billions of dollars** from their retirement accounts. And year after year, most people follow the same path: **Take the RMD in cash and move on.** Not because it's the best choice. But because no one ever tells them there's another way. **[The "Default" RMD Isn't Your Only Option.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e1111645/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsejFCdFd5WA/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWd8iA/sbue2c1e900)** Financial institutions make it easy to withdraw cash. Too easy. But simple isn't always strategic. Taking your RMD in cash may:
* Increase taxable income
* Force you to sell assets at moments that may not
align with your plan
* Reduce the overall portion of your wealth that remains invested

And yet... **[There's an IRS-Approved Alternative Most Retirees Never Hear About.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e1111645/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsejFCdFd5WA/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWd8iA/sbue2c1e900)** Few realize that **RMDs can also be taken "in-kind."** Meaning: instead of withdrawing cash, you can receive _certain assets directly_ without liquidating them first. No, it doesn't eliminate taxes. But for many savers, it may help them:
* Preserve their long-term allocation
* Avoid being forced to sell during volatile markets
* Strengthen diversification, depending on their strategy

It's fully IRS-allowed... but rarely mentioned in traditional planning conversations. **Before You Take Your Next RMD, Ask Yourself:**
* Do I know _most_ IRS-approved ways to satisfy my distribution?
* Am I selling assets when I don't want to - or at prices I don't like?

## Dallas Hotel Worker Fired for ICE Video
A 20-year-old college student working for a valet company at the Hilton Anatole in Dallas was fired after posting a TikTok video in which she said ICE agents were [staying at the hotel](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkb2uozAQhZ_GdI5sY_4Kim3o7rZbosEeg5XBjswkJG-_Iq9wy9GnOUefzr-f-QcixbT-hR1Hfoc8JzwPQmYs85YZ6czljiXEgh7WEt2T-DkbZVqptNR29hDpM9vKj4vyg65w1F3b14NRQ19towpD33gV-t4FBUvj_YJ159EvbhkMYBXHK0xpbbVRum5vunam60LXNGCDgyCsQh85lxtvyPiGI9Anv7DcXN4rGjfmxyHqP8JMwkzned7OAHBBYSYoHB2hMNPlJcxE2QEJM3kggkO6_Ez8uf7yDkl-NeUjHxzTKjneOd_lK3rMEohwRS9PKOmC0aGEFRMfcovEOUlIwPnbZfpO2rZf6mAX2YFurwvlUEMjB2vqwTTWuhaqMvrHGYni0XbCqnWHSF8t_t0Yr9H8DwAA__9Zkp_Q). Her Jan. 7 post has garnered more than 2.7 million views. "_Quite frankly, I don’t really care if I lose my job_ ," [said the woman](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMZ2R1_jHULi4hi7XXok29hKsbGJkNiF5-1PyCn890oy--XeaT5g53y9_8UZBXkuZ73TsTCJU57UI8VHqleqSKyW81BwfLI_ZGttrAxrcnDDze3ZNCmeTRmgogO-HbrRmHJo1IJzRRhfjYLyJbnAAS3QdGBr6cwLf5PApMwAOrIGub6GL1vvF__ygWyIuyhlKWUptZSWhF-4Lv8uTahvLreGwimy76v4oOyk7HcfRxrWW-ydVdvpwlJ2wSo5Myk4JmXHXT2QS_WVpyVcpV50j6S9ZW7BjB8a327o1NaTtyMx5771y5nLDzN9p-d1hz2D_BwAA__8qpoA8), who identified herself as Gia. "_I care more about your families and about unity_." Although she’s "normally a pretty quiet person," she decided to post the video after learning about the shooting of Renee Good in Minneapolis earlier that day. After posting the video, a manager for Gia's employer, Towne Park, asked her to take it down. When she refused, she was terminated for [violating](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0M2K2zAUBeCnkXc3SPL_QotAMd1MoVDo0txYV7aILAXpJpp5-5J5ha4PHM53_n6sH-iDj_svPMnwp0trpFoCMVNej8QUasp3ys5nsrhnvz0DP1ct9QBSgepWiz58rV1jzU3aWTVk1DhM7azlPDWHmR3i7Lap79tpkHbasFV6Gm_U21vXTm3jzbtMKtUpLVU7XFS76XF0Y99j5zZ0opNkPad84YOYPrG48JVelC9bOptgDuZHEe1V6EXopdZ6OUt8Z0IvFOFZhF7eKKGXxAdloReLIWCBmk6M8E0DlzKwv3O6w8tbSlAxRx93SA78RoA7RS6ADIcPnCJgRE6BhF4ww_Wq_vz--ePRZGMf1YfgyzCKTu4n-vC9k__v3ZfR_wIAAP__q-qRJA) the company's "business conduct policy." A GoFundMe campaign she launched has raised more than $4,000. An ICE agent reportedly complained to hotel staff when he saw Gia filming him. Hilton, which was criticized when one of its former franchise partners canceled reservations for ICE agents in Minneapolis, [issued a statement](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uqzAQhJ_GdEa2MX-Fi9vQ5banRMZewioLjswGkrc_Iq9wqpW-1Yxm5uc23jwSbvf_fgXH7zmNG5w7ATPkcUkMdKb8gDxjhujvGcOL-DUaZRqptNR2jB7pM9oiuknFXhfgdNt0VW9U3xWLiwBdXVUTzGAmBbavbWtMPUVb9V2YdIHuMlNaW22UrppSV8G07dzWtbdz8LOwCiJyyiUvwPD2-0yfdEAuQ1oLcgvzcxfVP2EGYYbzPMsw7VeL6y_M8JUIM1zoOinzIr9Qnmn1m1yQOG3Sb54TgcQAck8BPckVInp5YPYkD4yQJOOD00OYocguPk8kwr1phVX31SN9E_Hfdjyc-Q0AAP__cUuKxw) saying they "respect the privacy of all our guests."
## 30 Years Since Amber's Abduction
Yesterday [marked 30 years](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuozAQRb8GuolsYyAUFGno3kpbPG2JJvYYrNgmGpvw8vcr8gtPmu6MztW9_77mL_TBp-UPRhrLj9vmREcOVArxvG6FwrHxg9h5JosLe7OHss9KqA6EBKlniz68Z13b8S7sIGsaZd9dm0GJ4VqvoxC2s0jm3nZ9e9Vdp666cXJoRKt7Y2Xtx1MmpNRSCdl0F9kY1feub1vUzqCrtCDry8aXslKhH8wuvLcX8cVssQ7jWsozV82tUlOlpuM4LjGnk1VqogR7rtT03O_BG8joqLwBkwWKxAsl4-nkCyViDJWaMN6JAQNxgYj8yNAIeBNyBp_gEw_nfd5WXIgjJjCYCZgi-pRhT3kLL7KnjeF2k9_D4_tvzaN9Hj4En7u-0mKJ6MOnQvnd8K9R_Q8AAP__0MqaVQ) since 9-year-old Amber Hagerman was abducted while riding her bike in Arlington. Her body was found four days later. While her killer has yet to be apprehended, her death led to the creation of the nationwide AMBER Alert system, which has facilitated the safe return of more than 1,200 missing children. Following Amber’s death, her family and members of the community [began pushing](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOgyAURb8Gdxh4KNYFi9m462xnaZ7wUFKUBrG2fz9pM38w23uTk3vPz3W8Yohhm79xJVOePo0bnXukUiiPSyoUz5RvlH3I5HDOwR6xHCMI0FxILpvRYYivsamcmYTrZUVGdvqiehD9pVrM1OpeOaSJhAXqFZCXYLUC0LrpRVsF84YJKRsJQipdS2Wh63zXtth4i541glwoKddloUJP3H18pQfl2qa1imYp5b4z9cVgYDCc51lvk3X-fNcMhvcfBkNMFiOD4QPgfyHyG724D_ORiYeN4zpR5gvOlFfcuMWd-JFn2vkjzCHiZomXxO85FbKF2yVEl2ljMKhedyCAwVBl4-5niDHsumONmFcM8TO1_E_ww8BvAAAA___ZLpE6) for alerts about missing children over the radio. Local broadcasters partnered with law enforcement, and in 1998, 8-week-old Rae-Leigh Bradbury became the [first child recovered](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAQRU-Ds2pBgY0dEGzibDbd0CpD0Y0W2yPA4-nbr7xXmPhLT_-9Px_LB6Wc9udv2ti173gsO181c2tcltfROF9H-cslpsKBniX5M7dzQYkDSAXKLIFSfi-mC26VYVIdO2WHUU8op7F7ubUPKFfjraWVImq2xljrEU3oV619l9wNk0oZhVLp4aG0R2uj7Xsy0VMURnJI7SiP9uLG31Rjfh9fXB7-2LrsXq19VqF_CZwFztd1Pa5IdI8CZyot-cwC59tL4IwS3kylQk27Z4ip1Ab19J5rjWcG2lYuQJlLg1TryQHSDlTuSO3Yb8JooZc4rqonMGYyYFQMMIWhB_TE0zSOXsvQFRc-r5RzqoMVRj43Svn_5_az0l8O_wUAAP__CqGR1A) with the aid of the alert system. In 2003, President George W. Bush signed legislation that established national standards for the AMBER (America's Missing: Broadcast Emergency Response) Alert system, which [has been adopted](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGO6yAQgOHT2B0RYGygoHhNurx2S2tiBoMWG4QncXL7VfYKW__SV_xft_kGKad9_Q8bOnqFMu94HhmJsM2xEOaztG9sITX0sLa0PDI9ZsnlxLhgQs0eUn7Pqvfuzr0VPTqhJzNYya3poxsVjjZobcwSAK2e9GjvYxBSaT6EYPvkPhgXQgnJxTBdxLBIrYMeR1BhgdApjj5RaReKSPiCI-R3eWK7LGXrs4tE9eiGf528dvJasdSMn9TJ6xmBWIRacUfPqDDY7thYhBXbBjsTwphBc9M35-uZck7HpDvF1w1S_uXpb1OeTv4EAAD__4kOdjA) in all 50 states. Arlington police are still looking for Amber's killer, who is believed to be a white or Hispanic man in his 50s or 60s. ## Miller Proposes Agriculture Freedom Zones
Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller has [proposed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGuozAQRb_GdI48A8FQUGzj7m27JXLMEKxnMBoPj-TvV6TYH9hyRlf36Oj--Rq_fExxe_72Kw3ymvO40VkSiRCPSxZKZ-Zv4jkyTf7JMRxJjhENttqAhmacfEzvsamm4WGmHioawLZd3aPpu2oZ-kewCJ6m1pvO1h3aOnR3mG0PQIBUxeEqMwANoIG6vUEd0NrZ3u--mYOfVWNoipL5JgsJvXyZ0zv_EN9CXqs0LCJ7UfUvhU6hO8_zlo7HI4fvvKW40ZVS6Ipkfit0l97n9EIK3cVW6AwodFArdB-A_mfKpENe11hKzBux3jnvuVDRe_Kblnw9hILoQxc9e141-y0smqnkgwMVPXNetY968uJ1oE2IFbqug6aBBoyxCl3Fw7SfMaVYWqsa81x9TB89-b9Rfgb8GwAA__84EaI9) the creation of federal or state-designated Agriculture Freedom Zones to protect farmland from the proliferation of data centers. Miller's [plan](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0MGK2zAQxvGnkW8KkqzE9sGHZalOzVIobY9mIo2coWMrSLPJ7tuX5tAX6P3j48f_13k5AzHt6xtsOMtHLsuOj8YognW5FkF-lPoba6aKCdZK8Z3lfXHGnbSx2volAfHn4rs0X0yabIezHU5jPzkzjd11Bh_tZczgR9tHvEw5weTycYrOj0ccU0fz3zNjrbfO2P50sH10w5CH4xF8jpCVN5hISj3IFQU_oGX-LHesh1i2jueryK2p_kW5oFx4Dv5BKx7WclcuvOGj6S933KUpF16qUGRULlgzeKtceC3bRq1R2bHqMzFj1a_A3PSPW9n1dwFBDXvSARNWYP0VV2oMUmrTUvS3WgSj6J8kwDp0dU63BzFTOw3Km3UD4qdX_q_yfXZ_AgAA__8Nc5TY), announced Monday, would prioritize marginal land and underutilized commercial property for the development of data centers or renewable energy projects. Companies that build on those sites would be eligible for property tax incentives and capital gains tax deferrals. "_The unchecked spread of data centers onto prime farm and ranchland is a real and growing threat to our food supply_ ," Miller said. "_Once you pave over good farmland, it is gone for good_." In a [recent interview](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE9jMo9sg_kJHGxC9m26IWrsBqxpMLJ7hpnbr9grbFyqUr3352f6gUjxWH_Djo4_S5oOvAohM-ZpS4x0pfzEvMSMAdYc_Yv4NRllWqm01M0UINJ3aqrgZhUGXaHTXdvXg1FDX21uaAcbWhz6BuceOpitCiFYa-3Q9TroKrp7TGndaKN03T507U3XLZ210CweFtEoDJFTfvCGjB8oC33TG_PDp70itzGfRdS_hBmFGZ_8KXcgzHiTCDNS8kDCjCUGuUcizPLM6UwFizzwkjEgFMlJzkBweJSMfpNrThdvEo4g8ysD3R1GzzEdVXbhvCJRLG0nGrXuEOnfGf4_hW9n_gYAAP__YDCI9A) with an Abilene news outlet, Miller acknowledged the importance of data centers for job creation and national security. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. subject: Suburban taxes continue to rise
body:
News + editorial | Broad + Liberty Weekly Reads | | | |
---
| | | Good morning, and welcome to _Broad + Liberty_ 's Wednesday Weekly Reads!

As always, to stay up to date on late-breaking stories and analysis, [subscribe to our daily email list](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=602dc1afc8&e=b7b3eddce2) and get the best of _Broad + Liberty_ delivered straight to your inbox.

# [**1\. Philly suburbs pay Pennsylvania’s highest school taxes, new report finds**](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=e29b60bbd0&e=b7b3eddce2)
_By Beth Ann Rosica_ Homeowners in the Philadelphia suburbs are paying the highest school district taxes across the commonwealth, according to a new[ _report_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=530549f6b7&e=b7b3eddce2) by the Independent Fiscal Office. Residents in the collar counties are experiencing annual tax increases — and not just school taxes. For suburban taxpayers, the pressure comes from three directions: school districts, county government, and local municipalities. The increased tax burden trifecta places Bucks, Chester, Delaware, and Montgomery Counties as the most[ _expensive_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=4a01bde2f5&e=b7b3eddce2) places to live in the Commonwealth. **Why It Matters.** The increased tax burden trifecta places Bucks, Chester, Delaware, and Montgomery Counties as the most expensive places to live in the Commonwealth. According to the report, the collar counties have the highest school district taxes in the state by a large margin. The median school tax burden for a homeowner in Pennsylvania is $2,700, but the range varies widely with the high end at over $5,000 and the low end under $500. Chester County has the highest median school taxes at $5,386, followed by Montgomery at $5,009, Delaware at $4,952, and Bucks at $4,909. These four counties are a category unto themselves as the next highest county is Northampton at $3,571, which is roughly $1,300 less than Bucks County. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=32a7004355&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# [**2\. The demise of the Post-Gazette**](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=b02ff9591f&e=b7b3eddce2)

_By Jon Delano_ In southwestern Pennsylvania, most people have had a love-hate relationship with the _Pittsburgh Post-Gazette,_ the 240-year-old newspaper that abruptly announced the end of its long-term affair with the residents of this region, effective May 3. In the days since the rather impersonal videotaped announcement to employees, dozens of writers and commentators have both excoriated and sympathized with the demise of a newspaper whose byline proclaims itself, “One of America’s Great Newspapers.” **Why It Matters.** I’ll let others closer to the operation discern whether the striking employees themselves, corporate mismanagement with millions spent on union-busting, changing markets and audiences for newspapers, or just plain spite at losing court battles caused the closure of the _Post-Gazette,_ a local fixture since 1786. However you slice and dice it, it is a loss for Pennsylvania’s second largest city and a region that makes or breaks the Commonwealth’s politicians in statewide elections – and, thus, heavily dependent on accurate, fact-based news coverage. This news means that Pittsburgh will become America’s largest city without either a daily printed or digital newspaper.
---
|
---
|
# **3\. Lightning Round**

* [_From the Editors: A functioning republic needs a functioning news media_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=054e543e52&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Local Iranian Americans back their countrymen as protests continue_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=2ae763cbe2&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Thom Nickels: A Philadelphia history for the 21st century_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=c5c67c8243&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Paul Davis: Operation Absolute Resolve_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=dadfce3e6c&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_D’Orsie + Scanlan: Dads join the fight to protect girls’ sports_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=ffdcdce3dd&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Emily Greene Brey: Pennsylvanians want affordable health care, not more Obamacare_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=3cb451eb5e&e=b7b3eddce2)
* [_Ben Mannes: ICE shooting exposes America’s willful amnesia on law enforcement_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=e8a771e2bb&e=b7b3eddce2)

# **4\. What we're reading**
As Governor Josh Shapiro launches his reelection campaign this month — and quite possibly prepares for a presidential campaign in 2028 — he and fellow Democrats tend to focus on the _stuff_ the governor has “gotten done” here in Pennsylvania. But while Shapiro will no doubt tout the speedy reopening of I-95 in Northeast Philly, _UnHerd_ writer Ryan Zickgraf notes that the city where Shapiro spends most of his time, Harrisburg, is going rapidly [_from bad to worse_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=0caa237579&e=b7b3eddce2).

**Chapter 9 - Swinging and Missing**
Okay, I've been talking a lot about my spare time. What the heck was I doing for work and money in my twenties? Good question.
After law school, I was a lawyer at a big corporate firm, Davis Polk and Wardwell. Pretty soon, I had two thoughts:
1\. I am getting better at this job.
2\. I hate this job.
I went home for Thanksgiving to my parents that November and said, "You did not come to this country for me to do this. It's mind-numbing." My job at the time involved scouring hundreds of pages of documents looking for issues.
"What are you talking about Andy? You have a great job. We are very proud of you." Ah, Mom.
"You shouldn't be." I joked with my brother that when we were kids I dreamt of going into the woods and killing a dragon, not being the fucking scribe.
So why was I doing this lawyer job? Aside from the fact that I spent 3 years in school for it, it had to be the money.
I've had something of a funny relationship with money. I guess we all do. My parents were suck-the-meat-out-of-the-bones stingy. My Dad still takes joy out of getting through a day without spending a dime because he's found some free source of food.
When I was a kid, my Mom used to tell me how much everything cost so we would know how much she was spending on my brother and me. "You know how much this costs? You know how much that costs?" When I was a teen, I got fed up. I said to her, "How about this Mom, you can document everything you ever spend on me, and then when I'm older I'll repay every penny, and then we can never talk to each other again."
She was hurt. "Why are you so mean?"
"Okay, then if you're doing it out of love stop talking about it." I love my Mom.
Anyway, I've had a sense that I was going to need to work for money since I was a kid. As a teen I sold knives door-to-door - Cutco - and still remember the sales patter. Did I cut my hand with one of the ultra-sharp knives while cutting a bagel? Yes I did. Those things were a menace.
I worked at the school library at Exeter for $6.25 an hour. I was a snack bar worker frying chicken fingers at Josiah's during my freshman year at Brown. It was interesting how classmates wouldn't recognize you as soon as you put on a fast food hat and apron. I was a camp counselor during the summers.
Looking back, this was probably a little bit excessive. I was a middle-class kid. My parents at one point told me to work less and study more. But I always wanted to make my own money. I was on a partial scholarship to Brown from IBM but my parents often reminded me that they'd taken out a second mortgage on the house.
This extended past college into law school. When I was a 2nd year I got a summer associate job at a big firm. We were given a lunchtime reimbursement of $50 if we ate with a current lawyer. I know, it's a lot of money, and everyone used it to eat at fancy restaurants. One time I went to lunch with a couple of associates and they picked a fairly normal restaurant. The lunch entrees were 'only' $17 each, so I ordered two of them.
Everyone at the table was like, "What are you doing?"
Embarrassed, I said "Oh, I'm just really hungry" when the truth was I just wanted to make sure and spend all $50. Who wanted to leave money on the table?
I sensed everyone's eyes on me. I had to eat two lunches to avoid making it a thing. I moved the items around the dish to make it look done by hiding some remaining food under some mashed potatoes.
After law school I owed $110,000 in school loans. The firm I joined paid $120,000 plus a bonus of $45,000 to start. It seemed like an absurd amount of money to pay a 24-year old who hadn't done anything and didn't know anything. It was more than my Dad made, and he had generated 69 patents for GE and IBM. I felt like I was way too young to be making that kind of money but also that I shouldn't feel too committed. I didn't have kids, a mortgage or even a girlfriend. Whose dreams was I supporting?
So I left the firm after five months to try and start a dot-com company. Stargiving.com would raise money for non-profits, where if you clicked on an ad you'd help the charity and then maybe meet the celebrity. My parents thought I was a moron walking away from a six-figure job for my longshot little start-up. Turns out they were right, as we would throw in the towel about a year-and-a-half later.
I felt like a failure, lying on the floor of my little bedroom; I had moved in with my old doubles partner Andy to save money and was paying $1,080 a month. I had gone through my savings. My classmates were still making six figures practicing law. I had a net worth of negative $100,000. But I wanted to get better at becoming an entrepreneur.
I got a job at a mobile software company that ran out of money a few months later. One of my colleagues moved into the conference room with duffel bags of his stuff and was showering in the office. "You're living the dream!" I said to him, trying to be positive. He glared at me. I found another job working at a healthcare software company that made health records digital.
Given that I'd by then been a part of two companies that had gone under, I started looking for side hustles. I tutored students in standardized tests. I also began promoting parties under the name "Ignition NYC" with a few partners. We would throw big parties in Tribeca.
Throwing parties started with a simple but compelling question. A friend of mine asked me one night as we shared tales of rejection, "How do we become cooler?"
I answered, "We throw parties."
He said, "We can't do that, we live in tiny apartments with roommates. That won't look cool."
I said, "Then we use a lounge or bar. If we get enough people, they'll let us use it for free."
The reality was even better; if you got enough people to show up, the bar would actually pay you a percentage of the bar and give you some drink tickets. You could throw a big party and give free drinks to your friends and even make some money if you could get a couple hundred people to show up.
That didn't seem that hard for a 26-year old in New York City. I enlisted a few partners. One was Mike Skinner, Miika's roommate in Brooklyn who was the drummer for his band. Mike was cool. The other was Amy Engelhardt, who had grown up in the town next door. Everyone had a crush on Amy. The last was Gunny Scarfo, our resident tech guy.
If you want to become an entrepreneur, it turns out throwing parties is a great way to start. We had some phenomenal parties including one that drew 500 people on New Year's Eve in 2003. Everyone was desperate for something good to do on New Year's Eve, which is a holiday everyone secretly hates. Sort of like Valentine's Day.
I had three jobs for about 4 years; healthcare startup guy, tutor and nightclub promoter.
I was single for just about all of these years. One problem for me on dates was that I was very frugal. I lived on protein shakes and yogurt, so it was tough for me to switch gears to treat a woman to a nice meal. Look on the inside and believe in me, ladies! When I met a woman who didn't like me I thought it was because I wasn't successful enough. Meanwhile it was probably just me being insecure or a cheapskate.
Did I mention that I still owed six figures in law school loans? I started calling my loans 'my mistress' because it felt like I was sending checks to support a phantom family in another town. I hoped they were living a good life.
As you can tell, the book is a bit different for me and tells stories I never could before. I hope you check it out and pick up a copy!

| **About Eva and her race:**
Eva Lopez Chavez is a doer; where Western grit meets bold, democratic representation and a track record of making things happen. Known to many as the Salt Lake City Councilwoman or a project manager helping deliver housing and real solutions, she’s built a career on action, not talk. Today she’s stepping forward as a candidate for Congress, ready to fight for the communities that raised her. The new Utah 1st Congressional District encapsulates the bluest precincts of Salt Lake County. It’s a district Kamala Harris won by over 23 points in 2024 and a new D+13 baseline that is hungry to support a new generation of leadership.

# [Authoritarian fear is working](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=184353170&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg0MzUzMTcwLCJpYXQiOjE3NjgzOTk5NDIsImV4cCI6MTc3MDk5MTk0MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.arsUnFzJf2u2W_70-sh1V87NCADyi6QkXpTIksfAjQ4)

| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
