Friend, **Today, the Senate plans to vote on a War Powers Resolution, which would require Trump to get congressional approval before taking any more military actions against Venezuela.** Last week, the Senate voted 52-47 to advance the resolution, with 5 Republicans joining Democrats. **But Trump was apparently furious at the Republicans who voted with Democrats and since then has been pressuring the Republicans to vote no when it comes to the floor.** In response to Trump’s ire, Republicans are considering using Senate rules to table the vote altogether, claiming that the resolution does not qualify for expedited status because there are not currently U.S. troops on the ground in Venezuela. **We need to stop this authoritarian president from ordering another illegal military strike.** Our Senators need to hear from us now. [**Will you sign the petition to urge the Senate to stop Trump’s imperialist war against Venezuela?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9HWtiGz5LuqdYdydHcioHirQguUKYAAdhn_94MGw2MYWY6TQ9Xcp_dH0-ce_8OlVOPaT78rsQIa-jn79H-pZQ_6-iasrw6gwE_ZdHmTRejRpHwFlLQlZeoU5uV9JJ4a8qmpyIM61qgOHWrmggcCyfeUoRAnkeIK9GoWKbzrMEphb1e-2jO4sR22zqIVSFXSDoqJuJsCJwfNbESf60akFCgGoeLaKXl-pUzncdTWYmL8ClpHOvF1JsNmWKj5GVFPRe3_VeUnGD-wxKni3GntOOUCipLQ4rFtpJCyTxP0dzJQzpsYjvXHpkkDzgvprRXK2QPaGQ6ZNn3wPhG-zIm4Gm73d8bB6ZIvp-jxo5yARgIneG1PBHC4nGeRRl8G-7LpfoP9g2iLc-5cNU5U4iRANXK35z720NsHYePGURENykGAtL01DU2-xdFTxIdNXl6tCL/4na/o0YsZV-vQJWkVlIGRupTFg/h1/h001.S6eYUxUJHIbaE5WtrrtcDO6KWscVDYx8IbXorLR_K-I) | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9HWtiGz5LuqdYdydHcioHirQguUKYAAdhn_94MGw2MYWY6TQ9Xcp_dH0-ce_8OlVOPaT78rsQIa-jn79H-pZQ_6-iasrw6gwE_ZdHmTRejRpHwFlLQlZeoU5uV9JJ4a8qmpyIM61qgOHWrmggcCyfeUoRAnkeIK9GoWKbzrMEphYMrHdS7PQlCUaeBj0y7Tg6OTsS2X3I7NyqYqSVTxXmJFqZhipEyHDy3_JUnRIqg9xRUUvH5OffUUyBzAITMuky5sr_jl_ZyAXbTC3jfDC7VOe_aNUbXb8Fkgq2x1PC59Zmqtat-boSFzdbz5DIoxoQIXUsx8O5eRXtv1e5PLJhGbekg-Mlg7BFjF_qG5elfwWo-AXo0TKH6QG_pbCVVzfmQ8iFicBNCMr_CyiWJJ6sGdu2u6TIRQ1IAU1WyY5R_3NPwxpy4OLyUqB___7ALx-G/4na/o0YsZV-vQJWkVlIGRupTFg/h2/h001.SPeDB7wDoW61zbs8rTCQsvmcTQ7HpJGOUFRPGcbUuHI)

If enough Republican Senators stand up to Trump and pass this Venezuela War Powers Resolution, reclaiming Congress’ authority to authorize war, we then have to pass it in the House of Representatives. But it’s not just Venezuela where Trump is illegally wielding power. He is also threatening to invade Greenland and other countries, so Congress must block other imperialist wars as well.
I’m leading the fight to ban Congress members from owning stock in weapons corporations, and I’ll keep demanding our government fund our communities’ rather than endless war.
Half of each year’s nearly-trillion-dollar Pentagon budget goes to corporations, which donate to many of my colleagues. Fossil fuel corporations are also deeply entwined with our federal government, and Trump has been clear that he’s attacking Venezuela for its oil.
Together, we’ll keep demanding a government for the people, not corporate profits.
In solidarity,
Rashida

clean_body: I’m standing against Trump’s unconstitutional and imperialist war on Venezuela. | | | Friend, Today, the Senate plans to vote on a War Powers Resolution, which would require Trump to get congressional approval before taking any more military actions against Venezuela. Last week, the Senate voted 52-47 to advance the resolution, with 5 Republicans joining Democrats. But Trump was apparently furious at the Republicans who voted with Democrats and since then has been pressuring the Republicans to vote no when it comes to the floor. In response to Trump’s ire, Republicans are considering using Senate rules to table the vote altogether, claiming that the resolution does not qualify for expedited status because there are not currently U.S. troops on the ground in Venezuela. We need to stop this authoritarian president from ordering another illegal military strike. Our Senators need to hear from us now. | If enough Republican Senators stand up to Trump and pass this Venezuela War Powers Resolution, reclaiming Congress’ authority to authorize war, we then have to pass it in the House of Representatives. But it’s not just Venezuela where Trump is illegally wielding power. He is also threatening to invade Greenland and other countries, so Congress must block other imperialist wars as well. I’m leading the fight to ban Congress members from owning stock in weapons corporations, and I’ll keep demanding our government fund our communities’ rather than endless war. Half of each year’s nearly-trillion-dollar Pentagon budget goes to corporations, which donate to many of my colleagues. Fossil fuel corporations are also deeply entwined with our federal government, and Trump has been clear that he’s attacking Venezuela for its oil. Together, we’ll keep demanding a government for the people, not corporate profits. In solidarity, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib** Date: Wed, Jan 7, 2026 Subject: Demand an end to Trump’s war against Venezuela: To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, Were you one of the thousands of Americans who came out to emergency anti-war protests the past few days? I joined some of my constituents at a recent protest. Venezuela has the largest oil reserves in the world, and Trump’s not hiding it: His illegal attacks on Venezuela—which have already killed over 150 people—are about stealing oil for billionaires’ profits. Rather than informing Congress as is legally required, Trump instead informed U.S. oil company CEOs before the military attacks. This is oligarchy! This U.S.-forced regime change in Venezuela has already driven up stock prices for fossil fuel and weapons corporations. Trump and his donors will likely personally benefit financially. Some of my colleagues in Congress will also benefit from these unlawful military actions in Venezuela—whether through stocks and investments or through direct donations from companies that will profit off this. They need to hear from us now. For much of our country’s history, our government has destabilized other countries’ governments in order to control their resources and install U.S.-friendly leaders—often dictators. These imperialist actions have undermined democracy in other countries and violated human rights that are affirmed by international law, such as the right to self-determination. They also undermine U.S. democracy. The American people want our taxpayer dollars to fund healthcare, housing, food, and other basic needs—not bombs or endless wars. At the recent emergency protest I attended, my constituents held signs with messages such as: “Defund the Pentagon, fund human needs!” Last month I voted NO on the annual military budget, which unfortunately passed and authorized nearly a trillion dollars for death and destruction—about the same amount that Congress cut from Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act. We must keep pressuring lawmakers to stand with the American people, not military corporations. Thank you for taking action. Together, we must continue pushing the U.S. government to comply with international law and respect everyone’s human rights, including our rights to self-determination, healthcare, housing, and food. clean_body: Enough is enough. We cannot have rogue, lawless government agents killing people in our communities. | Peter, enough is enough. We cannot have rogue, lawless government agents killing people in our communities. But that is what ICE is doing – with the full, vocal support of Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem. It’s the latest in a long series of violations of our Constitution, our safety, and our trust. We deserve to live without state violence from state police. That’s why I am an original co-sponsor of the Articles of Impeachment for Secretary Noem. I’ve co-sponsored these three articles: 1\. Obstruction of Congress: Secretary Noem violated her oath of office and broke federal law by obstructing Congressional oversight and withholding funds appropriated by Congress. 2\. Violation of Public Trust: Secretary Noem violated the due process of American citizens and directed agents to commit illegal and unconstitutional acts. 3\. Self-Dealing: Secretary Noem abused her office for personal benefit and steered taxpayer dollars to associates. Under the Republican House and Senate, impeaching and removing Secretary Noem is a long shot. But we have to try. Using ICE and Customs and Border Patrol Agents to kill Americans is horrifying, immoral, and yes, fascist. The time to pull out all the stops is NOW. Thank you so much 💙 – Emily P.S. Since the White House attacked me last week, I’ve had protesters at my house, and I’ve received – many of them violent and disgusting. Thank you to everyone who has reached out in the last few days. Peter, I just checked our fundraising numbers from last year, and I was _stunned._

**$18.35.** That was our average donation in 2025.

I’ve ALWAYS put people first because that is who I represent. **Since Day One, our movement has truly been people-powered, people-centric, and proud of it.**

Thanks to small-dollar donors and supporters like you, I’ve been able to run the campaign we deserve: one that values Gen Z as the legitimate powerhouse we are. One that isn’t a piggy bank for shady special interests. One that counters fascism and hate with community and love.

So, I need to shout out every single small-dollar donor who has helped build this movement. _But we cannot slow down or get complacent._ That’s why I’m asking for your support today.

**Every single penny matters, Peter. And with your support, I can keep fighting in Congress and expand our movement to flip Florida blue.**

[**_Together, we’ll be the movement that takes Florida back from fascism. Brandon

Brandon Herrera

| | |

| | Friends,
As an elected county prosecutor, my responsibility goes far beyond standing in a courtroom and putting criminals behind bars. I am entrusted with upholding more than 500 constitutional and statutory mandates, protecting my community, standing up for victims, and advocating for meaningful, positive change.
Today, I want to share a few accomplishments I am especially proud of.
First is the work I have done with K9 victim advocates. I have had two K9 advocates serve in my office. Our first was a Black Lab named Reagan, and today we are proud to have Stryder. My office was one of the first in the state to incorporate a K9 victim advocate, whose sole responsibility is to support children and young adults who have been victims of some of the most serious crimes imaginable.
In 2018, I had the opportunity to work with my state representative at the time, now Congressman Tom Barrett, to pass HB 5645. This legislation allowed K9 victim advocates into courtrooms across Michigan. Reagan and Stryder have not been limited to Eaton County. They have traveled to Michigan State University, Oxford, and other communities to support students and families grieving after major tragedies.
Learn more about K9 victim advocacy:
* [Eaton County therapy dog visits Oxford High School](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZevr0BToQAismtaIt5VhjKFfqVaYyLK9a1m2395c2QA-u_I71VeUpfU2EY8nycRGOThuWhkdfCPHLOkMDXsNOzJAcFPjwRBqs1ARm-88SpLIt6jxwE2XYW_c1HjoXKlubYDbDqy3yu8KbI21wcwYIiFvyswZjwD3hziEYcD82Kqbwp9uVzkpHJOX5PBBCjzdpv&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)
* [Lawmakers endorse courtroom support dogs](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZe6NwdFfx4SOjx9wRMiloSph44PHhUWD8kOh-sjfuzHQdUH4FuliQxllAszWBasrZO1YORJBjOtQ0AEAclWV2gcUHUVBaKNWwJkiIXbuvuli0Oe4S0Yatj6XiNY_BsCSSZkRRNg51XwXxUFM4JkVHlMCwwzF3pAtrCkWF-Sdhlk5w_fFEu6c5Y2Q==&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)

I have also worked closely with a good friend, Xavier DeGroat, and the Xavier DeGroat Autism Foundation to help pass laws that bridge the communication gap between law enforcement and individuals with autism. Xavier is an outstanding young man and was the first individual with autism to intern at the White House, working for President Trump during his first term. Together, we have advanced additional initiatives to improve communication between law enforcement, government agencies, and individuals with special needs, making a real difference in people's lives.

Learn more about our autism advocacy work:
* [Xavier DeGroat Autism Foundation initiative](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZeaftl3vD39kKTumvP_YbnjVbJHZD1jCWP2NqzY08HtGSvKJw74TLHimMx6gfoQrUdWzX1fVLoI3ENF7XbmNzl7ECCukzmSVMGnGXSR1SQYLrDaKogRFLGTmvPuN3dqYHOII0NqkLItkdcKfgC7HmvPw==&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)
* [Community impact and legislative advocacy](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZe9ctH9IqY_6nJT-v84mdE5txx6_unqFFaXsMEq6tfjNj-Bb4HO_vN7XfDZpRKISj2WAxlHLHEVpyErSqhtvGHJF1q6VGZNiowcs7tKC1Jhtkj-L9wMG5Vg1hp866fTOP3ko00a_EwBcAHbkkmlySgcQ==&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)

Lastly, when members of the Legislature attempted to pass laws that weakened the criminal justice system and put public safety at risk, I stood with House Republicans to fight back. I worked closely with Judiciary Chair Graham Filler to oppose these progressive reforms, often stepping in to do the work our Attorney General should have been doing. As a result of my efforts in both the Legislature and the courtrooms of Eaton County, I was honored with the Champion for Crime Victims Award, presented by the Crime Victims Foundation.
Learn more about my work defending crime victims:
* [House Republicans' plan to protect crime victims](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZe7tOHiF55IoWnGCoB6V3ymGyiUegA-p2-C8UburvZgvZyAffNdcx6W1jysZTil6sYATVMBkesy3OFvzYkttJrd9e1GyvSYv7Y4Ova0bvxp3yUeQbdAzzQYLZFC7B1wHs69MCH8jAX9HPfO44dDT_Wpibvm-QTivBWNgZO5-2UGJMHxlptsR7C3A==&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)
* [Champion for Crime Victims Award recognition](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Uh3yuLCUS0b4H7L-0IM2XXj4uBFCS7LMud_Rx4m4eFY7UIAMmJSXUDLS7BUZFEZewCollzmJYPajLHKwcsPS16IoqIJHmkCCIkR3ZffLNQ62qXgwHXcgatKHoizRMmdIHlJueHWETKWAwzRld34NUO74CgBWv3NLLefY3f3RZ4RqIyA5xoEGOSPGnSev6BgdOj4JJGE1bmFKqmFqgAJtCQ==&c=nP0ObUW-_wLBpyk_GiSsndp7w_qXx_ilBqhXzNATKptxzeHgsXMBBw==&ch=HLY3_4dJ2E-tIN1PsanRggPXMTPIkr-A_J5WoQMK1PCtfPHktbrWbg==)

What delegates need to understand is this: being Attorney General is about far more than standing at a podium and talking about who to sue next. It is about leadership, advocacy, and the courage to speak up for victims and the voiceless.
I have done that throughout my career as a prosecutor, and I will continue to do so as your next Attorney General.
Sincerely,
Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

clean_body: Leadership Beyond the Courtroom | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, As an elected county prosecutor, my responsibility goes far beyond standing in a courtroom and putting criminals behind bars. I am entrusted with upholding more than 500 constitutional and statutory mandates, protecting my community, standing up for victims, and advocating for meaningful, positive change. Today, I want to share a few accomplishments I am especially proud of. First is the work I have done with K9 victim advocates. I have had two K9 advocates serve in my office. Our first was a Black Lab named Reagan, and today we are proud to have Stryder. My office was one of the first in the state to incorporate a K9 victim advocate, whose sole responsibility is to support children and young adults who have been victims of some of the most serious crimes imaginable. In 2018, I had the opportunity to work with my state representative at the time, now Congressman Tom Barrett, to pass HB 5645. This legislation allowed K9 victim advocates into courtrooms across Michigan. Reagan and Stryder have not been limited to Eaton County. They have traveled to Michigan State University, Oxford, and other communities to support students and families grieving after major tragedies. Learn more about K9 victim advocacy: == == I have also worked closely with a good friend, Xavier DeGroat, and the Xavier DeGroat Autism Foundation to help pass laws that bridge the communication gap between law enforcement and individuals with autism. Xavier is an outstanding young man and was the first individual with autism to intern at the White House, working for President Trump during his first term. Together, we have advanced additional initiatives to improve communication between law enforcement, government agencies, and individuals with special needs, making a real difference in people's lives. Learn more about our autism advocacy work: == == Lastly, when members of the Legislature attempted to pass laws that weakened the criminal justice system and put public safety at risk, I stood with House Republicans to fight back. I worked closely with Judiciary Chair Graham Filler to oppose these progressive reforms, often stepping in to do the work our Attorney General should have been doing. As a result of my efforts in both the Legislature and the courtrooms of Eaton County, I was honored with the Champion for Crime Victims Award, presented by the Crime Victims Foundation. Learn more about my work defending crime victims: == == What delegates need to understand is this: being Attorney General is about far more than standing at a podium and talking about who to sue next. It is about leadership, advocacy, and the courage to speak up for victims and the voiceless. I have done that throughout my career as a prosecutor, and I will continue to do so as your next Attorney General. Sincerely, Doug Lloyd Eaton County Prosecuting Attorney Candidate for Michigan Attorney General 👉 == | | | | | == == == == 1.16.26 - Ionia County GOP Meet & Greet == == == == == | | | | == == == == | | | | | == | | | | Doug Lloyd for MI Attorney General | PO Box, 80536 | Lansing, MI 48906 US | | | | | | | |

Arizona is _ground zero._

If Democrats get even a little bit of power back in 2026, they’re going to turn our state into a political punching bag and a testing ground for their next wave of insanity. And that starts with flipping seats like this one. They don’t hate me because of my “tone” or because I’m “too conservative.” **They hate me because I’ve done the job they refuse to do:**

I fought cartels.

**January is Caucus Season**
[ Pledge your support](https://substack..QkTauwPdryAkQqekhvOpX8J1_Wmy79Xo-SFfjxjc3LM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=184557069)

Throughout most of Connecticut, Republican towns recently held their Republican Town Committee (RTC) caucuses. These caucuses appoint representatives from each town and district to serve on local Republican governing bodies. Despite how consequential this process is, most people in Connecticut have no idea it even exists--or how profoundly it affects who ultimately appears on the ballot.
This is the gatekeeping mechanism of local politics. _**Before anyone can run for office, before a name appears on a primary or general-election ballot, it must first pass through the town committee structure.**_
Each town is divided into districts, and each district is allocated a specific number of RTC seats. Candidates for these seats are technically elected, but in practice turnout is often limited to friends, family, and party insiders who know when and where the caucus is happening. The process itself is antiquated, relying on obscure newspaper notices and minimal public outreach. _**There is almost no media coverage --Republican or Democrat-- the Democratic Town Committees follow a similar system.**_
**Collectivism Over Individualism**
The current caucus system frequently favors collectivism over individualism. Slates are assembled behind the scenes (**and sometimes multiple slates**), and challengers who have the chutzpah to run independently are often discouraged or opposed.
**Competition is not discouraged as** the rules still allow for competition: if **ANY** challenger is nominated, seconded, and brings enough people to vote, they can win. **Popularity still matters --at least on paper.**
What's striking is how small these elections usually are. In most districts, caucus attendance ranges from 15 to 25 people total, including the candidates themselves and their family members. Typically, four to six people are competing for a handful of seats. _**Occasionally, during moments of genuine grassroots energy, turnout can surge to 75 or even 100 people per district that show up to vote --but that is the exception, not the norm.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ce05129-3d67-4822-a6fd-3395de11928d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Over the past several years, many towns have experienced "old guard versus new guard" struggles within their RTCs. _**These internal battles have produced reversals, takeovers, and sustained infighting. It is a troubling dynamic: people who largely share the same values and principles unable to reach consensus --or unwilling to accept the legitimacy of popular support.**_
_If someone can persuade more people to show up and vote for them, why shouldn 't they have a seat at the table?_
When internal divisions become severe, the caucus can spill into primaries. These primaries are often not driven by ideology, but by unresolved personal or factional disputes that should have been addressed internally long before a ballot was printed.
**What RTC Service is Not**
It is also important to understand what service on an RTC is not. Serving on a Republican Town Committee is not the same as serving on a Board of Education or on formal municipal bodies such as taxation, planning, or zoning commissions. RTC members are not setting tax rates, approving developments, or managing schools. An RTC's role is far narrower and far more political: to participate in the monthly workings of local party governance--endorsements, strategy, messaging, and candidate development and support.
**When will the fighting end?**
The broader problem is that the Connecticut Republican Party too often ends up fighting itself. _**In a state dominated by a Democratic supermajority, internal warfare only weakens an already disadvantaged minority. Every ounce of energy spent battling fellow Republicans is energy not spent challenging Democratic dominance, expanding the party 's base, or developing competitive candidates.**_
**How will this year 's caucus shake out?**
Over the next several weeks, the impact of these caucuses will become clear as the new mix of RTC members settles in across the state. Whether you won a seat, lost one, or never ran at all, the takeaway is the same: local politics matters. These small, overlooked meetings shape the future of elections in Connecticut.
**You don 't need an appointed vote to make a difference on an RTC--but you do need to show up and bring a few friends to the next RTC Meeting.**
In the words of Bruce Hornsby - "That's Just the Way It Is" until the Tonya Hardings and the Nancy Kerrigan's start fighting for Team Connecticut

body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Today, I want you to hear this directly from me: I’m running for re-election to serve as your California Attorney General.
I’ll level with you — over the past few months, I’ve been carefully considering how I can best serve Californians as we face unprecedented challenges.
I’m grateful to work with so many people who care so deeply for this state and its future. And as we look toward that future, my resolve is firm — our fight against relentless attacks from this Trump administration, escalating corporate greed, and rising costs requires a leader with battle-tested experience.
Over the past week, we’ve all watched a dystopian horror come to life.
The murder of Renee Good in Minnesota was terrifying and tragic. And the immediate push from our federal government to gaslight Americans and distort the narrative to serve themselves reaffirmed something I feel in every fiber of my being: in this moment, my place is here as Attorney General — shielding Californians from the most brazen attacks on our rights and our families.
Over the last five years, we’ve built a wall of protection around this state. A legal fortress around our freedoms and our values that not even the most unlawful president can tear down.
Over the last year we’ve sued Donald Trump more than 50 times — and we’ve won. Again and again and again.
Together, we have proven that when California fights, we win.
This is why I have decided to continue my campaign to earn another term as your Attorney General. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
We are at our strongest against the rising tides of tyranny when we stand together, each of us clear-eyed and committed to the roles we must play.
When we turned on our TVs last week to see federal agents gunning people down in their own neighborhoods while at the same time the President attacked innocent children, vulnerable families, and child care providers, it reminded us all that Trump’s attacks aren’t just a policy dispute, they are an assault on the California Dream itself — the idea that everyone here should be safe, free, and treated with dignity.
My vision for the California Department of Justice is that we remain the nation’s largest and most powerful check on the abuse of power.
We aren’t just defending the status quo. We are securing the California Dream for the next generation.
Together we fight, together we lead — and together, we must finish the job.
I am fiercely committed to doing whatever it takes to stop unlawful power grabs from the federal government, defend our immigrant communities, protect reproductive freedom, safeguard our environment, hold greedy corporations accountable, keep our communities safe from gun violence and fentanyl trafficking, and stand up to abuse of power wherever it appears — and to do all that, I’ll need you with me.
Today, please become a founding donor to my 2026 campaign for re-election to the office of Attorney General. No amount is too small — your contributions add up to make all of this work possible. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
If you’ve saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
DONATE $10 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?express_lane=true&amount=10] DONATE $25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?express_lane=true&amount=25]
DONATE $50 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?express_lane=true&amount=50] DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?express_lane=true&amount=100]
DONATE $250 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26?express_lane=true&amount=250] OTHER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
The fight is far from over, and the months ahead will demand preparation, courage, and the resources to act swiftly when Californians need us most.
Thanks for being here with me.
—Rob

name: DNC Grassroots Fundraising Team
subject: We’re pulling back the curtain
body:
---
Derek, In the last few days, maybe you’ve gotten an email that starts like this: _Is there ANYTHING we can say to get you to contribute?_ To pull back the curtain on how online fundraising works, the reason so many campaigns and organizations use this phrase is because it’s effective for raising money (we’ve even seen that ourselves). But in this moment — with so much going on and so many valuable causes to give to — we know that it is not enough to just ask for your contribution. There is probably _not_ one magic thing we can say. We have to earn your trust and support, every single day. We take that responsibility seriously. So if you choose to support the DNC, here is exactly what your donation helps us do:
* **Register new voters.** We just launched a first-of-its-kind partisan voter registration push focused on winning back young people. This year, we’ll work to register hundreds of thousands of new Democrats and train the next generation of organizers to do it.
* **Invest in every single state party.** Every month, we invest $1 million across all of our Democratic state parties to ensure Democrats have the support they need to show up and compete _everywhere_.
* **Allocate resources to the place they’re needed most.** The DNC is the organization best positioned to invest in the races where our support can make the biggest difference. And with so many elections this year, that job is more important than ever.

As you can imagine, all of this takes a HUGE amount of resources. It’s our team’s job to raise the money that makes it possible. clean_body: Derek, In the last few days, maybe you’ve gotten an email that starts like this: Is there ANYTHING we can say to get you to contribute? To pull back the curtain on how online fundraising works, the reason so many campaigns and organizations use this phrase is because it’s effective for raising money (we’ve even seen that ourselves). But in this moment — with so much going on and so many valuable causes to give to — we know that it is not enough to just ask for your contribution. There is probably not one magic thing we can say. We have to earn your trust and support, every single day. We take that responsibility seriously. So if you choose to support the DNC, here is exactly what your donation helps us do: Register new voters. We just launched a first-of-its-kind partisan voter registration push focused on winning back young people. This year, we’ll work to register hundreds of thousands of new Democrats and train the next generation of organizers to do it. Invest in every single state party. Every month, we invest $1 million across all of our Democratic state parties to ensure Democrats have the support they need to show up and compete everywhere. Allocate resources to the place they’re needed most. The DNC is the organization best positioned to invest in the races where our support can make the biggest difference. "Good vs. Power: From Venezuela to Minnesota Streets" drops as America grapples with fundamental questions about who we are and what we're willing to tolerate. Chuck Rocha and Mike Madrid don't shy away from the hard stuff in this season premiere. Instead, they lean into it with the unflinching honesty that's made this podcast essential listening for anyone trying to understand Latino politics and American democracy.
### When Policy Becomes Violence
Fresh from visiting Rwanda's genocide memorial, Chuck returns to witness another American tragedy: 37-year old Renee Good shot three times in the face by ICE agents in Minnesota.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..jk6pPITOJYDsc9mxGzWerFHdCMhy-YdJFl8wpMCHxWw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=184562713)
Mike Madrid doesn't mince words: "A woman lost her life yesterday morning, Chuck, mother of three, a poet, **killed by her own government without due process**."
This wasn't an accident. "There's no way this could have ended any differently other than violently when you triple the size of ICE, when you flood the streets of America with masked law enforcement officers that are untrained and armed," Mike explains. "This isn't the last time this is going to happen folks. It's going to happen with regularity. That's the point."
The administration is offering $50,000 bonuses to recruit new ICE agents. Mike's assessment is chilling: "It's like the Proud Boys full employment act."
### From Venezuela to Greenland: The New World Order
The episode tackles Trump's intervention in Venezuela head-on. Mike cuts through the noise: "What Trump is trying to say is it's our sphere of influence. So we have the rights to go in because we want their stuff. If that sounds exactly like what Vladimir Putin used as justification to go into Ukraine, it's because it is."
Canada is building up armaments and recruiting militia because of America's aggressive posture. Think about that. Canada is preparing to defend themselves from us.
"We're Russia," Mike says flatly. "We're behaving like Russia now, both foreign and domestic."
### Latino Politics 2.0: From Representation to Results
Mike delivers the episode's most important insight: "The chapter in Latino political history that was overly focused on representation is transitioning to Latino 2.0, which is gonna be focused on results."
Two politicians who overperformed most with Latinos? Bernie Sanders and Donald Trump--"old white dudes with populist messages."
"The community doesn't need Latino representation. The community needs Latino results," Mike declares. "And if our people aren't gonna follow the data, follow the results and start providing it, they will go vote for somebody else. And you know what, brother, they should."
His challenge to Latino legislators: "Quit looking to your progressive, culturally progressive members of your caucuses and kneeling to their agenda. Grab them by the scruff of their neck and say, we will take care of all of your social progressive issues once people can feed their kids. How about that being the priority?"
### Why It Matters
As Texas primaries begin in six weeks, Chuck and Mike are tracking contested races that will determine the direction of the Democratic Party. Pennsylvania's 7th District: a white union firefighter backed by Bernie leading against a Latina candidate in a 27% Latino district.
These aren't abstract debates. They're about whether we prioritize working-class economics or symbolic representation. Whether we choose good or power.
Mike reminds us: "The warriors have to lay down the shield and the sword and beat them into plowshares as the good book says. There has to be a time and a season where things move on. But the work is not done yet."

name: Justin Riemer - RITE President
subject: RITE Celebrates Supreme Court Victory Affirming Candidate Standing in Election Challenges
body:
7-2 ruling says candidates have standing to challenge state election laws in federal court |
---
| |
---
| | **RITE Celebrates Supreme Court Victory Affirming Candidate Standing in Election Challenges**
**WASHINGTON, DC** – Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE), a non-profit organization that supports litigation to protect the rule of law in elections, today celebrated a major victory at the Supreme Court in _Bost v. Illinois State Board of Elections_ , where the Court [ruled](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=5a25a1b47b&e=ea91f782ea) 7-2 that candidates have standing to challenge state election laws in federal court.

RITE filed [three amicus briefs](https://riteusa.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc5917dfc5aa19cc3795efbb2&id=ddd6dcefc5&e=ea91f782ea) supporting the petitioners throughout the litigation, urging the Court to clarify that candidates harmed by state election practices can seek judicial review.

The case arose from a challenge to an Illinois law allowing absentee ballots to be received and counted up to 14 days after Election Day. While the lower courts dismissed the case on standing grounds, the Supreme Court reversed, holding that candidates suffer concrete injury when state rules undermine the integrity of the electoral process and that they have the right to bring such challenges in federal court.

“This is a major win for the rule of law in our elections,” said RITE President Justin Riemer. “Too many courts for too long have avoided grappling with legitimate and meritorious challenges to election rules by dismissing cases on standing grounds. RITE is proud to have joined with Center for Election Confidence and Honest Elections Project to support this important litigation and help achieve this victory.”

The Court’s opinion provides much-needed clarity on candidate standing in election law disputes, resolving a question that has divided lower courts and created uncertainty for candidates seeking to challenge allegedly unlawful election practices.
###

name: Eliza Walton
subject: Big oil made a mess in our state. Let’s make them pay to clean it up...
body:
https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=sU1/LKMMDJxkays+QldHv/4Tu+pP4Lx/z6Bih2OgGlnomrvu720o6W78FNc2INRd9mkM9Rcr3A/MFP/HoTeWyOZe4L/q5YZizYLMoxmM54WFtav9UTP/415ArW7q2uM4 [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=sU1/LKMMDJxkays+QldHv/4Tu+pP4Lx/z6Bih2OgGlnomrvu720o6W78FNc2INRd9mkM9Rcr3A/MFP/HoTeWyOZe4L/q5YZizYLMoxmM54WFtav9UTP/415ArW7q2uM4]
Peter,
The worsening climate crisis tramples our basic values of safety, wellness, and fairness. For decades the world’s largest polluters have knowingly dumped climate pollution into our air and water without any accountability, all while banking massive profits. Under current policy, we’re stuck paying for most climate-driven costs with our dollars and our health. It’s well past time that polluters pay for recovery, adaptation, and resilience costs, not Oregonians.
Add your name now [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=sU1/LKMMDJxkays+QldHv/4Tu+pP4Lx/z6Bih2OgGlnomrvu720o6W78FNc2INRd9mkM9Rcr3A/MFP/HoTeWyOZe4L/q5YZizYLMoxmM54WFtav9UTP/415ArW7q2uM4]
That’s why we’ve enthusiastically joined the Make Polluters Pay coalition, a diverse group of organizations fighting for the Climate Resilience Superfund bill that is coming back in the short session.
Oregon’s Climate Resilience Superfund bill requires major, out-of-state fossil fuel companies to pay their fair share for climate-related disasters and to fund solutions that prepare our communities for future impacts. Importantly, funds will be prioritized for wildfire preparedness and recovery and climate resilience projects, such as:
* Preparing homes, buildings, powerlines, and more to be wildfire safe;
* Sustainable, preventative work to cut down on wildfire risk in the first place;
* More energy-efficient cooling and home weatherization to protect us from extreme heat and smoke, while lowering utility bills;
* Rebuilding better and more resilient after major floods or wildfires;
* Combating water shortages with more efficient irrigation equipment for Oregon farmers.
To hold these massive polluters accountable, your state legislators need to hear from you. Here’s how you can join us and get involved today:
Sign the Make Polluters Pay Petition
We’ll be hand-delivering this printed petition to Salem. Add your name now to ensure your voice is there with us.
Add your name now [https://secure.ngpvan.com/Txv-EIYKCk6bDzVIkhWfpg2?contactdata=sU1/LKMMDJxkays+QldHv/4Tu+pP4Lx/z6Bih2OgGlnomrvu720o6W78FNc2INRd9mkM9Rcr3A/MFP/HoTeWyOZe4L/q5YZizYLMoxmM54WFtav9UTP/415ArW7q2uM4]
Craft Your Personal Story
Everyone has been impacted by climate change, so everyone has a story to tell. To prepare for the Make Polluters Pay Advocacy Day in Salem (Feb. 16), you're invited to a night of community building and storytelling on January 27. At this workshop, you’ll build confidence in sharing your story by learning:
* The basics of storytelling, including time to practice
* Storytelling best practices and a helpful story framework
* How to use your story to advocate for change
RSVP now [https://secure.ngpvan.com/2gxiMZv_HUCVO3r0_Sx_1Q2?contactdata=sU1/LKMMDJxkays+QldHv/4Tu+pP4Lx/z6Bih2OgGlnomrvu720o6W78FNc2INRd9mkM9Rcr3A/MFP/HoTeWyOZe4L/q5YZizYLMoxmM54WFtav9UTP/415ArW7q2uM4]
Make Polluters Pay Storytelling Workshop
WHEN: Tuesday, January 27 from 6 to 7:30 p.m.
WHERE: Zoom
The economic costs of fossil-fuel-driven climate change are here and have to be paid. Together, we can change who foots the bill. It’s time to make polluters pay for the resilience that Oregonians need.
Sincerely,

To hold these massive polluters accountable, your state legislators need to hear from you. Here’s how you can join us and get involved today: Sign the Make Polluters Pay Petition We’ll be hand-delivering this printed petition to Salem. Add your name now to ensure your voice is there with us. Add your name now [] Craft Your Personal Story Everyone has been impacted by climate change, so everyone has a story to tell. To prepare for the Make Polluters Pay Advocacy Day in Salem (Feb. 16), you're invited to a night of community building and storytelling on January 27. At this workshop, you’ll build confidence in sharing your story by learning: The basics of storytelling, including time to practice Storytelling best practices and a helpful story framework How to use your story to advocate for change RSVP now [] Make Polluters Pay Storytelling Workshop WHEN: Tuesday, January 27 from 6 to 7:30 p.m. WHERE: Zoom The economic costs of fossil-fuel-driven climate change are here and have to be paid. Together, we can change who foots the bill. It’s time to make polluters pay for the resilience that Oregonians need. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Most retirees miss out on bigger Social Security checks—leaving billions unclaimed. Friends, I’m extremely proud to share that Leader Hakeem Jeffries has named me parliamentarian of the House Democratic Steering and Policy Committee.
What does that mean? Fair question! First, it means I’m the newest member of Democratic House leadership, which I’m very excited about.
But more importantly, it’s a major opportunity to help shape the priorities and strategies of House Democrats. Right now, it’s crucial for Democrats to be bold, united, and both responsive and forward-looking.
We’re two weeks into 2026, and this year has already been incredibly hard for our country. ICE is on a rampage. Donald Trump has kidnapped a world leader and launched illegal and unauthorized military operations. And costs are still out of control.
So even though we’re in the minority right now, Democrats must leverage every tool we possibly can to stop Trump from shredding the Constitution and further eroding our democracy.
We also need to be focused on the future — building a proactive agenda that earns back the trust of the American people by responding to their urgent needs.
America is in an unprecedented moment, with high and rising stakes. As part of Democratic House leadership, I’ll work every day to make sure our work reflects the experience and talent of the Democrats elected to serve.
I know this community has many thoughts for House Democrats, so please reply to this email to share with my team what you think leadership should know going into 2026.
Thanks and talk soon,
Sara

Hello -
My name is Mary Peltola, and I want to share with you why I've made the decision to run for the United States Senate in Alaska — and to ask for your support as we begin this journey together.
But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to become a Founding Donor to our campaign, please use this link to split a contribution today:
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/pbp-em-20260114?refcode=ema20260114/founding-donor**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260114.QqgC5X&refcode=ema20260114-240602&t=3&akid=240602%2E444211%2EGHS3rQ)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260114.QqgC5X&refcode=ema20260114-240602&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=240602%2E444211%2EGHS3rQ)**
Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.
When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.
Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.
Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.
So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just _crushing_ Alaska families.
And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. _They don’t even believe us._
They're focused on their own wallets — not ours.
And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.
It’s why our prices are rising, and our heating bills keep going up. All while the health care and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.
I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.
Systemic change is the only way to bring down grocery costs, save our fisheries, lower energy prices, and build new housing Alaskans can actually afford.
Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again.
My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.
But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.
I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.
**This is going to be one of the closest Senate races of the next election, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to win this race... and that is together.**
So I am asking:
[**Please contribute to my campaign for the U.S. Senate and Powered by People today to become a Founding Donor. We are looking for a huge number of donors to get our campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260114.QqgC5X&refcode=ema20260114-240602&t=5&akid=240602%2E444211%2EGHS3rQ)
**[Donate $3](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260114.QqgC5X&refcode=ema20260114-240602&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=240602%2E444211%2EGHS3rQ)**
Thank you,
Mary

subject: Bradstock Volunteer Action Items
body:
Good Evening,

Thank you all for your time and effort. We could not do this without your help! As we enter this busy campaign season, here are this week's action items and upcoming events:

**Action Items:**

\- **Host a Meet & Greet:** Please consider hosting a candidate Meet & Greet. These can range from small gatherings to larger events. They are vital for boosting Alan’s name recognition and fundraising.

\- **Veterans for Bradstock:** We are looking for veteran volunteers to join this group. If you are interested, please email me your t-shirt size so I can order a shirt for you. We hope our veterans will inspire others to learn more about Alan by wearing these shirts at campaign events.

\- **Petition Training** : On January 22nd at 6:30 PM, we are hosting a virtual training to explain the petition process. Please register here: [Zoom Registration Link].

**Upcoming Events:**

-**Somerset Fire & Ice Festival: **Alan will be serving his white chicken chili on Saturday, January 17th, from 3:00 PM to 5:00 PM at the American Legion in Somerset. Please stop by and visit with Alan afterward if you have time.

\- **Westmoreland County Campaign Kickoff** : This event is scheduled for February 4th. I have attached the invitation to this email. While donations are not necessary for our volunteers, please RSVP to Christina Proctor if you plan to attend. Regardless of your attendance, _please share the event on your social media platforms._ Help us get the word out!

Thank you again for being a crucial part of this campaign!

Best,
Kate
\--

Kate Rullo

Over the weekend, I began seeing photographs coming out of Iran of young women lighting cigarettes from the flames created by burning photos of the Iranian Ayatollah.

What a brave, bold act of defiance against a tyrannical, murderous government who terrorizes its own people and chants “Death to America.”

**Iranians want freedom.**

Iranians want fundamental human rights, and they are protesting by the thousands to defy the regime that has spent decades murdering Iranians and murdering Americans as the world’s largest state sponsor of terror.

subject: My mentor, Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Phil Weiser for Colorado
body:
Her memory is a blessing we honor with action.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123320946/595074478/1239926708?refcode=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ms=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDU5YzBmMS03NGYxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AHQvfeWd8cDlY6-hj3abKE2111uuslayKuuwrpV8e4U=&emci=541b73e8-d2f0-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&emdi=9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ceid=51844520) Friends, when I clerked for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, she taught me through her words and actions about advocating for others. Justice Ginsburg inspired me to always fight injustice, stand up for our freedoms, and promote equality and justice for all. And as we face unprecedented threats to these values, I think often of how she would respond to them and how she would want me to. **[Justice Ginsburg taught us to fight for what we believe in — and do it in a way that others will join us. That’s my mission as I run to be your next governor. And today, I’m humbly asking for your support so we have the resources to stay on track toward our fundraising goals and win in June.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123320947/595074479/-246109695?refcode=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ms=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDU5YzBmMS03NGYxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AHQvfeWd8cDlY6-hj3abKE2111uuslayKuuwrpV8e4U=)** | | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123320948/595074480/-246109695?refcode=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ms=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDU5YzBmMS03NGYxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AHQvfeWd8cDlY6-hj3abKE2111uuslayKuuwrpV8e4U=)
---
When I see the Supreme Court being asked, “if you're born here in the US, are you really a citizen?”, I know Justice Ginsburg would fight passionately against this attempt to claw back the 14th Amendment protections our nation established over a century ago.
**I will always fight back against lawless attempts to strip Americans of their citizenship.**
When _Roe v. Wade_ was overturned back in 2022 with the Supreme Court’s _Dobbs_ decision, I recalled my mentor and knew how appalled Justice Ginsburg would have been.
**I will always defend Coloradans’ right to abortion access and reproductive freedom.**
When the Supreme Court stands by its atrocious _Citizens United_ decision, which RBG called the Court’s worst recent decision, I know that we cannot just wait idly by.
**I will always fight for a political system that represents people, not corporations and the wealthy few — and that’s why I am championing a proposal to prevent corporations from donating to Colorado campaigns.**
And when we witness the Bully-in-Chief violating the rule of law in so many other ways — whether he’s coming after Colorado for our gold-standard election system, bypassing Congress to set tariffs that cause chaos for Colorado businesses and families, or sending ICE to spread terror in our communities — I know RBG would demand that we rise to the occasion. **I will never give in to this administration’s lawless bullying without putting up a fight.**
**[Justice Ginsburg taught me valuable lessons about using the law to stand up and deliver for all people. As your next governor, I will put those lessons into action. And to win in June, I need your support today. If you’re able, can you chip in $25 now to help keep us on track?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123320949/595074481/-246109695?amount=25&refcode=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&ms=ea.9459c0f1-74f1-f011-8194-000d3a11f903&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5NDU5YzBmMS03NGYxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=AHQvfeWd8cDlY6-hj3abKE2111uuslayKuuwrpV8e4U=)**

clean_body: Her memory is a blessing we honor with action. Friends, when I clerked for Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, she taught me through her words and actions about advocating for others. Justice Ginsburg inspired me to always fight injustice, stand up for our freedoms, and promote equality and justice for all. And as we face unprecedented threats to these values, I think often of how she would respond to them and how she would want me to. = | | = When I see the Supreme Court being asked, “if you're born here in the US, are you really a citizen?”, I know Justice Ginsburg would fight passionately against this attempt to claw back the 14th Amendment protections our nation established over a century ago. I will always fight back against lawless attempts to strip Americans of their citizenship. When Roe v. Wade was overturned back in 2022 with the Supreme Court’s Dobbs decision, I recalled my mentor and knew how appalled Justice Ginsburg would have been. I will always defend Coloradans’ right to abortion access and reproductive freedom. When the Supreme Court stands by its atrocious Citizens United decision, which RBG called the Court’s worst recent decision, I know that we cannot just wait idly by. I will always fight for a political system that represents people, not corporations and the wealthy few — and that’s why I am championing a proposal to prevent corporations from donating to Colorado campaigns. And when we witness the Bully-in-Chief violating the rule of law in so many other ways — whether he’s coming after Colorado for our gold-standard election system, bypassing Congress to set tariffs that cause chaos for Colorado businesses and families, or sending ICE to spread terror in our communities — I know RBG would demand that we rise to the occasion. Peter,

I’m going to be brutally honest with you.

Arizona is _ground zero._

If Democrats get even a little bit of power back in 2026, they’re going to turn our state into a political punching bag and a testing ground for their next wave of insanity. And that starts with flipping seats like this one. They don’t hate me because of my “tone” or because I’m “too conservative.” **They hate me because I’ve done the job they refuse to do:**

# Silver Smashes $90 As Miners Cash In
Silver **[surged past $90 per ounce for the first time ever](https://substack.com/redirect/ac4af308-dd82-4ae2-8e69-ef72af00a3fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on Tuesday, holding firm above the milestone Wednesday as industrial demand and market volatility fuel the rally, sending U.S.-listed silver mining stocks sharply higher in pre-market trading amid a 27% year-to-date gain for the metal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ac4af308-dd82-4ae2-8e69-ef72af00a3fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Record High Sustained:** Silver prices extended gains to trade around $90.55 per ounce, marking a historic breakthrough driven by its dual role as industrial and investment metal.
* **Mining Shares Rally:** Hecla Mining jumped 3.4%, Endeavour Silver 3.3%, and First Majestic Silver 3.2% in pre-market, with ETFs like iShares Silver Trust up 4.2%.
* **Industrial Edge Highlighted:** BlackRock's Evy Hambro notes silver's industrial focus differentiates it from gold, with prior rallies limited by rising costs until recent profitability levels.

# Trump blasts Powell as "jerk" doomed to vanish soon
President Trump escalated his feud with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Tuesday, **[branding him a"jerk" who "will be gone soon"](https://substack.com/redirect/2c8e940b-9a31-49fd-b3d1-e974f69c1ce0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** amid a DOJ criminal probe into Powell over Fed headquarters renovation cost overruns and congressional testimony, fueling widespread fears of eroding central bank independence even as top bankers like Jamie Dimon warn of inflationary risks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/2c8e940b-9a31-49fd-b3d1-e974f69c1ce0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Trump dismisses Dimon** **Warnings:** Trump brushed aside JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon's concerns that undermining Fed independence could raise inflation and rates, insisting Powell has "done a bad job" and lower rates are essential.
* **Pirro defends DOJ probe** **aggressively:** U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro rejected political motivation claims, stating her office pursued subpoenas after the Fed ignored repeated outreach on renovation overruns and testimony discrepancies.
* **Powell ties investigation to rate pressure:** In a Sunday video, Powell linked the grand jury subpoenas and indictment threats directly to administration demands for faster interest rate cuts rather than sound policy.
* **Bipartisan backlash grows rapidly:** Republican lawmakers and figures expressed alarm over potential economic fallout, with some vowing to block Trump's future Fed nominees until the probe resolves.

* * *
* * *
# Fed gov's mortgage fraud allegations to get a Supreme Court showdown
The Supreme Court will hear oral arguments next week on President Trump's bid to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over **[mortgage fraud allegations,](https://substack.com/redirect/be65fc3f-ff71-4340-b30f-57773e4bb00b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a case that could pave the way for ousting Chair Jerome Powell amid escalating clashes over interest rates and central bank independence.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be65fc3f-ff71-4340-b30f-57773e4bb00b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Supreme Court Date Set** : Oral arguments scheduled for January 21, 2026, in the challenge to Trump's removal of Governor Lisa Cook, testing presidential authority over Fed board members.
* **Cook Fraud Allegations** : Administration claims Cook misrepresented her primary residence on mortgage applications last year, though courts have blocked her firing pending the high court's review.
* **Powell Probe Implications** : A Justice Department investigation into Powell, including recent subpoenas over a Fed headquarters renovation and congressional testimony, raises stakes for potential removal if the Cook precedent favors the White House.
* **Independence at Risk** : Economists warn a ruling against Cook could erode the Fed's political insulation, influencing monetary policy and increasing chances of lower rates under Trump pressure.

* * *
* * *
# Apple Ditches OpenAI For Google AI Powerhouse
Apple has selected Google's Gemini models to power its revamped Siri and core Apple Intelligence features in a multi-year deal announced this week, **[sidelining OpenAI as the primary AI foundation](https://substack.com/redirect/e1605a17-6ed8-41f5-a048-b9e1c606f8ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** despite its earlier ChatGPT integration on iPhones -- a major win for Alphabet that pushed its market cap above $4 trillion and a stinging setback for the ChatGPT maker in the intensifying AI race.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e1605a17-6ed8-41f5-a048-b9e1c606f8ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Gemini Tops Benchmarks:** Google's Gemini 3 outperformed rivals including OpenAI's models on key industry tests late last year, prompting Sam Altman to issue a "code red" and rush out GPT-5.2 to mixed reception.
* **OpenAI 's Apple Snub:** Analysts called the lost core partnership a "huge loss" for OpenAI, especially after its prior ChatGPT rollout on iOS and perceived challenge to Apple via a Jony Ive hardware collaboration.
* **Google 's Strategic Edge:** The agreement positions Google's AI across most global smartphones (iOS and Android), letting Alphabet control AI disruption on its terms while boosting its cloud and dominance in the market.
* **Existing Ties Remain:** Apple emphasized no changes to its optional ChatGPT access for complex queries, maintaining a hybrid approach but clearly favoring Google's tech as the "most capable foundation" for future features.

* * *
* * *
# Meta **begins massive Reality Labs layoffs** shifting from metaverse to AI
Meta has begun **[cutting more than 1,000 jobs in its Reality Labs division,](https://substack.com/redirect/eb64245f-4361-4801-8e76-a3e6bab38649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** pivoting resources away from virtual reality and the metaverse toward AI-powered wearables and mobile features, as the costly unit seeks sustainability amid billions in losses.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eb64245f-4361-4801-8e76-a3e6bab38649?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Reality Labs Hit Hard** : More than 1,000 positions eliminated, representing roughly 10% of the division's 15,000 employees, with notifications starting Tuesday morning January 13, 2026.
* **Metaverse Dreams Scaled** : Company pivots metaverse efforts to focus on mobile devices while reducing aggressive VR investments, closing three in-house VR game studios including Armature, Twisted Pixel, and Sanzaru.
* **Heavy Financial Losses** : Reality Labs has incurred over $70 billion in losses since 2021 due to investments in VR headsets and virtual products that have yet to generate significant revenue.
* **AI Wearables Expansion** : Savings reinvested to accelerate wearables growth, including talks with EssilorLuxottica to potentially double AI smart glasses production capacity to 20 million units annually by end of 2026.

* * *
* * *
# Ford unleashes attainable Bronco RTR beast
Ford unveiled the **[2027 Bronco RTR at the Detroit Auto Show](https://substack.com/redirect/d5365102-ced1-4131-9ade-92403e08128c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on January 13, 2026, introducing a more accessible high-performance off-roader through its partnership with Vaughn Gittin Jr.'s Ready to Rock brand. Positioned as a stepping stone to the pricier Bronco Raptor, the new model blends rugged capability with street appeal using a 315-horsepower turbo engine.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d5365102-ced1-4131-9ade-92403e08128c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **RTR lineup expands dramatically** The 2027 Bronco RTR becomes the eighth Bronco variant and the second RTR model after the Mustang, featuring design tweaks and off-road upgrades for enthusiasts seeking performance without top-tier cost.
* **Accessibility drives strategy** Ford positions the RTR as a "gateway" to the elite Bronco Raptor family, with executives emphasizing its lower entry point compared to the roughly $80,000 Raptor.
* **Engine specs target balance** Equipped with a 2.3-liter turbo four-cylinder delivering 315 hp and 350 lb-ft of torque, it offers strong power while staying below the Raptor's 418-hp V6 output.
* **Pricing bridges key gaps** Expected to slot between the $51,475 Bronco Heritage Edition and the $19,995 Bronco Raptor, making high-performance off-roading more reachable for a wider audience.

| | Over the past seven years, Florida has delivered results. **We have more than tripled our rainy day fund, doubled our budget reserves, and retired nearly half of all Florida’s taxpayer-supported debt** , saving more than a billion dollars in principal and interest. Florida now has one of the lowest levels of spending per capita in the nation; and the fewest state government workers per capita of any state. **We have built the strongest economy in America.** For three years in a row, Florida’s economy has ranked number one in the nation. Hey folks,
**Don Lemon** and I went there. Epstein. Trump. Bill Clinton. Power. Accountability. And the absolute chaos that follows when a government refuses to tell the truth. The conversation turns direct early -- and it doesn't drift.
Here are a few moments you'll want to jump to (or rewind and watch twice):

* [**00:04:44**] Trump, Epstein, and why refusing to release the files tells you everything you need to know
* [**00:10:19**] The viral Sasha Riley allegations -- what we know, what we don't, and why misinformation thrives in silence
* [**00:20:31**] ICE, unchecked power, and how the death of an innocent woman exposed something far darker
* [**00:24:36**] "Good shoot or bad shoot?" -- why accountability matters, even (especially) for law enforcement

We talked about why transparency matters, how rumors fill the void when leaders lie, and what happens when institutions stop protecting people and start protecting themselves. This is a conversation about justice, fear, media failure, and what it means to actually tell the truth in public -- even when it's messy. **As a former CIA officer who’s worked overseas, I've seen democracies flicker out.**
Several weeks ago, myself and five other Members of Congress with service and veteran backgrounds made a video directly quoting the Uniform Code of Military Justice about the military’s responsibility to reject illegal orders.
In response, President Trump called for my arrest, trial and death by hanging.
**Last week I learned that former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, asked to interview me.**
This is on top of the FBI’s Counterterrorism Division’s inquiry at the end of last year.
As a former CIA officer, I've seen democracies flicker out. I’ve seen what life is like when a government is rigged. I’ve studied this kind of political authoritarianism in other countries where you can't criticize the guys in charge without getting a knock at the door in the middle of the night.
It’s hard to believe I am talking about it in my own country, and the knock is happening on my door.
I've always tried to be straight with you in these emails. When these threats happen, it requires a strategy -- because no American wants to live in a country where the president can weaponize the government against his perceived enemies.
[**So please: a contribution to my campaign today will help defend me from these attacks and allow me to keep fighting to defend our democracy.](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-26.79HKre&refcode=em260114&t=2&akid=2398%2E135344%2EiwvxBa)**

New Yorker: The Case for Dumping the Electoral College [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-end-electoral-college?refcode=011426_1&amount=25]
The Electoral College has been described as “ a loaded pistol pointed at our system of government. ” They warned that it created “a game of Russian roulette” because the way it distorts the will of the people could threaten our democracy.
We've already seen the popular vote loser win the White House five times, including twice in the last twenty years .
And this obtuse system of choosing a national leader led directly to the former President -- one of those five who lost the popular vote ( in 2016 ) but still won the office -- attempting to subvert the will of the people by twisting the Electoral College into a mess and when that didn't work, fomented a literal insurrection with supporters breaking into the Capitol Building to disrupt certification of the election.

body:
I retired from the United States Navy with the rank of Captain. Everyone who has worn the uniform of our country knows that rank is earned, not given.
#

Friends,
I retired from the United States Navy with the rank of Captain.
Everyone who has served in the military knows that rank is earned, not given.
I earned my rank flying into combat and launching into space.
The Secretary of Defense wants to take that rank away from me because I said something his boss didn’t like.
In the United States of America, that’s still unconstitutional. So, I’m suing him.
At the end of the day, Donald Trump and his Administration’s actions chill the rights of every military retiree, who could face censure, demotion, reduction in retirement pay, and even court-martial if they speak out against him.
I’m not going to stand for it.
