Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just _crushing_ Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. _They don’t even believe us._

They're focused on their own wallets — not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices are rising, and our heating bills keep going up. All while the health care and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

Systemic change is the only way to bring down grocery costs, save our fisheries, lower energy prices, and build new housing Alaskans can actually afford.

Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

**This is going to be one of the closest Senate races of the next election, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to win this race... and that is together.**

So I am asking:

I know your inbox is likely full of requests from campaigns and organizations talking about the new year and asking for your support. I hate to add another to that, but **_[can you give me a chance to make my case for why my campaign could really benefit from your help today?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123328286/595098877/819412648?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250,500&amount=10&refcode=email_011426_case&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTIzMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5ZDdlOWNmNC04N2YxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=kqnjcJ7j9-tCXse_L8NUWtDQyK1NCAJSXBnZL3uRqgE=)_** After the primary opened up and Bill Huizenga officially entered the race, I sat down with my team and set an ambitious plan for January so we can execute the strategy we’ll need to win. And that plan starts with hitting a higher fundraising benchmark so we have the resources to reach voters – _early and often._ **Here’s the bad news: our fundraising has slowed down quite a bit this week, and we’re pacing behind our January goals.** While we won’t have to publicly report our numbers at this point in the quarter, this mid-month benchmark is the first test to see if our momentum is growing at the scale that we need it to, or if our energy was just a fluke. And sadly, if we can’t keep up, we’ll have to scale back on our plans. **That’s the last thing we want to do.** I highly doubt that you woke up planning to donate to my campaign. But that’s what I need you to do if you can. We have a lot of ground to make up before tomorrow, but it all works when everybody gives whatever they can, whenever they can. **_[So can you please contribute $10 or whatever you can spare to help fund my campaign to flip MI-04 blue and retake our Democratic House majority? Griswold, county clerks urge Polis to reject clemency for Tina Peters ahead of appellate arguments
| | | | [](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
| | Hi friends,
**🚨 LIVE TODAY:** Rocky Mountain Voice will be livestreaming Tina Peters’ court hearing as [oral arguments unfold](https://link.email.joinrmv.) in her appeal, where her legal team is now asking the court to order her immediate release. **[Watch live and follow real-time coverage on our YouTube channel HERE [starts at 2:30PM MT].](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
Listen to today's Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.joinrmv.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.joinrmv.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.joinrmv.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Colorado faced rising public safety and policy tensions as Summit County’s sheriff [cut 13 positions under a trimmed 2026 budget](https://link.email.joinrmv.), highlighting strain on local law enforcement. Denver advanced a [ban on officers wearing masks](https://link.email.joinrmv.) during arrests, raising concerns about conflicts with federal partners, while a former Green Mountain High School [psychologist was convicted of sexually assaulting a child](https://link.email.joinrmv.). A new Common Sense Institute report found homelessness in Colorado is [driven more by drugs and crime than housing costs](https://link.email.joinrmv.), and in Aurora, an immigration resolution drew [warnings from the police chief](https://link.email.joinrmv.) and residents over public safety risks. The state is also preparing to enforce [new semiautomatic firearm training and eligibility requirements](https://link.email.joinrmv.) in 2026.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** The U.S. Supreme Court heard cases on whether states may [bar biological males from competing in girls’ sports](https://link.email.joinrmv.), a decision that could redefine fairness in women’s athletics. Meanwhile, a new commentary argues the real “insurrection” is the [surge in violent attacks on ICE agents](https://link.email.joinrmv.) enforcing federal law, warning that excusing such violence undermines law and order and constitutional accountability.
This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, January 14, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Griswold, county clerks urge Polis to reject clemency for Tina Peters ahead of appellate arguments](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
With Peters’ appeal heading into oral arguments, Griswold and the Colorado County Clerks Association put it in writing for Gov. Jared Polis: don’t step in.
The Jan. 13 letter carries three signatures: Griswold’s, Jackson County Clerk & Recorder Hayle Johnson’s and Colorado County Clerks Association executive director Matt Crane’s. In it, the group asks Polis not to grant clemency, warning that doing so would have consequences beyond Peters’ case.
“In 2021, then-Clerk Tina Peters coordinated the breach of her own election equipment in the nation’s first public elections insider threat,” the letter states, asserting that her conduct placed the security of Mesa County elections and public confidence in democracy at risk. The authors further argue that clemency would validate similar conduct in the future.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**[Aurora council immigration resolution sparks warnings from police chief, draws resident response](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Council targets federal enforcement:** Aurora City Council approved a resolution criticizing ICE for what it called unlawful and overreaching immigration enforcement, directing city staff to begin discussions on limiting cooperation with federal immigration agencies.
* **Police chief warns of public safety costs:** Aurora Police Chief Todd Chamberlain cautioned that scaling back coordination with federal partners could undermine crime prevention efforts and make it harder to hold criminals accountable, stressing that law enforcement cooperation has helped improve public safety.
* **Residents push back on sanctuary-style moves:** The resolution sparked public response, with residents organizing outreach and warning that reducing cooperation with ICE could harm community safety and strain already tense policing challenges.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
|
---
**[This is the real insurrection](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY MARK SALLEY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Violence against law enforcement is the real threat:** The commentary argues the true “insurrection” is the surge in attacks on ICE agents simply for enforcing federal law, citing reports of assaults increasing more than 1,300% and death threats skyrocketing by as much as 8,000%.
* **Double standard on law and order:** The author contrasts the treatment of January 6 protesters—none charged with insurrection—with today’s tolerance for violent attacks on federal officers, accusing political leaders and media of excusing lawlessness in sanctuary jurisdictions.
* **Call for accountability and renewal:** The piece urges Americans to reject disorder, support law enforcement, and pursue immigration policy changes through elections rather than violence, ending with a call for national prayer and repentance.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
[**Counties told to fix energy policy they didn’t create: Mesa commissioner pushes back**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | JANUARY 12** _Mesa County Commissioner JJ Fletcher said he wasn’t looking to start a political fight when he published a recent op-ed questioning Colorado’s rapid move away from natural gas. What he wanted, Fletcher said, was to put a practical concern on the record—one he hears repeatedly from rural counties._ __
[**El Paso County District Attorney Michael Allen Announces Run for Colorado Attorney General**](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | JANUARY 12** _District Attorney of El Paso County Michael J. Allen has declared his intention to run for attorney general in Colorado. Allen served in the Navy and is in his second term as district attorney for Colorado’s Fourth Judicial District. His announcement comes as the state grapples with rising auto theft, higher insurance costs, and continued overdose deaths.Allen framed the decision as a gradual one._____
[**Strategy First: Obey Before You Engage**](https://link.email.joinrmv.) **BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JANUARY 11** Before acting, consider who is guiding you—God or man. The divine plan or human influence. Or, good versus bad influence. We live in a world that prizes action. People, society, and negative influences often push us with “make the move,” urging us to take a shot, trust our instincts, and do what feels right.[****](https://link.email.joinrmv.)__

That’s why I’m looking forward to this forum... though I’m not sure all of my opponents will have the courage to show up and debate those issues head-to-head.
Events like this separate the real fighters from the rest. I’ll be there, ready to answer every question and lay out why I’m the best choice to replace Chip Roy and represent **YOU** in Congress.
Bring a friend or neighbor, pack the room, and let’s send a message that TX-21 demands bold, battle-tested leadership.
I can’t wait to see you in Kerrville!
For Texas,
Trey TrainorHusband, Father of 6Prover Conservative Fighter

clean_body: We might disagree about who makes the best rice, but it’s our diverse perspectives that truly empower us. | | | Peter, food is never just food. Our recipes embody our memories and our culture. We explore this through a one-of-a-kind show, Just Flavors — the first immigrant cook-off competition ever! In the Just Flavors kitchen, young people share dishes that shape who they are, where they come from, and remind us how much our food and culture bind us together. Our collective power comes from our different experiences. We might disagree about who makes the best rice, but it’s our diverse perspectives that truly empower us. name: Adam Schiff
subject: I’m standing with Mark
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY SCHIFF FOR SENATE
body:
| Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth could learn a lot about putting duty before self from Mark Kelly and the other brave veterans speaking out.
# [](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/61?t=1&akid=9414%2E5257348%2E0Cvw4p)
Derek,
Senator Mark Kelly put his life on the line to serve and defend our nation, as a fighter pilot and an astronaut. And he has always believed in putting the Constitution and his country first.
**I stand with him, and I am deeply proud of his courage to fight back against the Trump administration's baseless and dangerous intimidation tactics.**
Donald Trump and Pete Hegseth could learn a lot about putting duty before self from Mark and the other brave veterans speaking out.
I know too well what it’s like to be viciously targeted by Trump and to have this administration come after me.
They’ve come after me repeatedly, attacked me in the Oval Office and on Fox News, and even tried to launch a baseless investigation against me.
**For Mark, they are attempting to deny his decades of honorable and courageous service to the nation by threatening to demote him and reduce his military pension.**
Trump and Hegesth want to send a message to the generations of servicemembers who took an oath to this country that the administration will come after them if they say something Trump doesn’t like. It’s yet another attempt to chill people’s First Amendment rights, silence critics and censor speech.
**They aren’t going to succeed in shutting Mark up, and they aren’t going to succeed in intimidating any of us.**
[**I stand firmly with Mark and I am asking you to join us. Chip in to help Mark and me keep up the fight against censorship and intimidation. Together, we will continue holding Trump accountable.**](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/1014?c0=q12026_abs_em_kelly.peiHpg&refcode=AU_ABS_FR_TAN_GEN_AC90_20260114_PM1_V1_S1&%3Bemail=&t=4&akid=9414%2E5257348%2E0Cvw4p)

Help us continue to respond to anti-democracy attacks in key states.
|

MAGA has already wiped out 10 Democratic seats in red states. If the California map had been struck down, MAGA would have only needed 3 more seats to guarantee control of the House for decades to come--a feat they would have easily been able to achieve. Now that California's maps are set in stone, Democrats must continue going on the offense to counter MAGA's all out blitz. Every seat matters right now for Democrats. The math as it currently stands is not in our favor, but with each state that counters MAGA, the momentum swings back in our direction. name: Roy Cooper
subject: short note
body:
We can only win together.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/2365?source=&t=1&akid=349%2E124072%2E0T2uEk)
**Peter, we have hard work ahead of us.** _I know better than most how competitive our statewide elections here in North Carolina can be._ I know that winning them takes the dedication to meet voters wherever they are, the commitment to listen to what folks need, and the determination to see this work through. We’re in the midst of the hardest fight of my career, and I won’t be able to win without help and support from across the country. I don’t want to alarm you, and I won’t ever tell you that the sky is falling when it isn’t. That’s not the kind of campaign we’d run. But our fundraising pace has slowed in the last couple weeks, and we’re at risk of falling behind this month’s goal. **[If you’re able, please pitch in today, before our mid-January deadline tomorrow.](https://act.roycooper.com/go/4372?t=7&akid=349%2E124072%2E0T2uEk)** | **[DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/4372?t=8&akid=349%2E124072%2E0T2uEk)**
---
Thank you very much,
Roy Cooper
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/4372?t=9&akid=349%2E124072%2E0T2uEk)
* * *
Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

body:
Trump is leading us into a war with Venezuela
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/123331688/595111015/938567526?refcode=header&noskip=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyY2NkNTZkNi05M2YxLWYwMTEtODE5NC0wMDBkM2ExMWY5MDMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=3dQPn8Z8Ns5QWawfrKL97UGR1fMxDrB5idTLB0sCqxM=)
This is Congressman Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee.
President Trump is leading us toward war with Venezuela — without Congress, without accountability, and without the Constitution.
**Let me be clear: this is dangerous, unconstitutional, and unacceptable.**
The Trump administration has all but admitted the truth — this is about oil and control, not democracy. While Nicolás Maduro is a brutal dictator, that does not give any president the authority to launch a war or pursue regime change on their own. The Constitution is clear: only Congress can authorize war.
Instead of lowering costs, fixing health care, or helping families here at home, Donald Trump is once again steering the country toward another foreign conflict. We’ve seen where this road leads. Endless war. Lost lives. Trillions of taxpayer dollars wasted.
**_Congress must act immediately._**
**I am calling for a War Powers vote to block any unauthorized military action against Venezuela. And we need Republicans to step up and put the Constitution over party — before it’s too late.**
_If you believe no president should be able to start a war alone...

clean_body: Trump is leading us into a war with Venezuela = This is Congressman Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee. President Trump is leading us toward war with Venezuela — without Congress, without accountability, and without the Constitution. While Nicolás Maduro is a brutal dictator, that does not give any president the authority to launch a war or pursue regime change on their own. The Constitution is clear: only Congress can authorize war. Instead of lowering costs, fixing health care, or helping families here at home, Donald Trump is once again steering the country toward another foreign conflict. We’ve seen where this road leads. Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just _crushing_ Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. _They don’t even believe us._ They're focused on their own wallets — not ours. subject: Rob Lucero Knows How
body:
Rob Lucero is running for Congress because there is a serious, practical answer to how the United States can regain its manufacturing capability.

| | |
---
Hi Peter, Rob Lucero is running for Congress because there is a serious, practical answer to how the United States can regain its manufacturing capability. It is H.R. 5356, the National Infrastructure Bank Act of 2025. Before running for office, Rob helped develop this legislation as a private citizen. The bill would create a permanent national bank dedicated to financing large-scale infrastructure, advanced manufacturing, energy, transportation, and industrial projects. Not short-term stimulus. Not giveaways. Long-term, productive investment that rebuilds the physical and human backbone of the economy. This is how America can rapidly begin to regain its industrial capacity and the process knowledge that goes with it. By putting people to work building real things, at scale, with good wages and benefits. By reconnecting research, production, and skilled labor inside the United States. We invite you to learn more about Rob’s approach and why this bill is so important. Visit [https://www.luceroforcongress.com/platform](https://www.luceroforcongress.com/platform?e=39cdcb2fb7adda80e7fc66430579bb85&utm_source=luceroforcongress&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=lucero_knows_how&n=1) and read the section titled: **“Reindustrialize America – Lucero Knows How to Create Millions of New, Good-Paying Jobs with Benefits.”** The future of America depends on whether we choose to build again. Rob Lucero is running to make sure we do. Thank you for taking the time to learn more. Please let us know what you think about Rob’s proposals. **Team Lucero** **Rob Lucero****

I’m requesting your support in this critical battle to restore common-sense conservative values to Minnesota. I hold a Master’s from Harvard, a Master’s Certificate from Johns Hopkins in Security and Nuclear Deterrence, and an MBA. But my proudest achievement is serving our country to make my parents, especially my mom, proud. I want to serve you in the U.S. Senate, fighting for the values that have made Minnesota and America great for generations. I’m starting this race with absolutely nothing , but because of the enormity of the race's outcome, I figured there is no harm in asking for your help. At the end of the day, my request of you will end in one of two ways: 1.) . 2.) you read this email without contributing, but you at least now know who I am. I’m not a career politician. I’m a regular guy from a working-class family who grew up playing hockey and answered our nation’s call on my 18th birthday in October 2001, just weeks after the 9/11 attacks. I joined the Marine Corps to defend our country, and as a Navy SEAL, I deployed nine times to over 70 countries, risking my life to protect our freedoms and way of life. Unlike Tim Walz, who retired from the National Guard before his unit deployed to Iraq, I never backed down from serving our nation during war. Minnesota is at a crossroads. Under Governor Walz and his lieutenant governor, our state has been dragged left by radical policies that fueled the violent unrest in Minneapolis in 2020, defunded our police , and burdened hardworking families with higher taxes and inflation. While our streets burned, the lieutenant governor pushed lawsuits against law enforcement, undermining the officers keeping us safe. This isn’t the Minnesota I grew up in—or the one any Minnesotan deserves. If you are reading this email right now and you don’t live in Minnesota, then I’m sure you’ll agree with me that every American must be represented by individuals in Congress who want to build a better version of the America we live in today—individuals of integrity. We have an incredible opportunity to elect a Republican to the U.S. Senate next year - something voters in this state haven’t done since they re-elected former Senator Norm Coleman in 2002. I’m the proud daughter of immigrants who fled Iran’s authoritarian regime of fear and repression. Arizona raised me, and I’m ready to continue the fight for everyone who calls it home.
I carried that fight from the United Nations, where I helped to deliver the historic Paris Climate Agreement, to Phoenix, where, as the Vice Mayor, I expanded housing options, invested in clean, affordable transportation, and created good-paying jobs.
And last year, I was sworn in as the youngest woman in the 119th Congress — part of a new generation of leadership.
I’ve held the powerful to account — demanding answers for Epstein survivors, and exposing corruption and insider trading at the highest levels. When Trump defied the Supreme Court, I went to El Salvador to defend our Constitution.
As Trump pours billions into ICE, I see the fear it creates in our neighborhoods. That’s why we trained thousands of our neighbors to know their rights, and worked with community leaders to keep families safe.
I’ve gone inside detention centers to demand humane treatment. And I’ve fought for my constituents — like Yari, a woman battling leukemia — demanding that ICE provide the care she desperately needs.
**Because no one should be left to suffer in U.S. custody.**
I’m leading the fight against Big Oil’s greed — so families pay less for their utilities. I don’t take corporate PAC money. I don’t own or trade stocks.
And with my affordability agenda, we’ll make housing, health care, and AC bills more affordable. This is the fight of our lives — and Arizona is at the center of it.

And with my affordability agenda, we’ll make housing, health care, and AC bills more affordable. body:

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. name: AOC
subject: They're relying on us giving up.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Hell no.
#
What the MAGA movement wants is for all of us to give up and say, “America has gone to hell in a handbasket, and we’re done.”
**No.**
If you are a hard-working, innocent person: **I have got your back**.
If you are just trying to make it in this world: **I’ve got your back**.
If you’re not trying to hurt anybody: **I got your back**.
It’s so important that we affirmatively assert that because, now more than ever, there are a lot of people who don’t know who they are safe with.
But when we speak up, we signal to others that there are people in this world who have not given up.
There are times when we are _not_ in positions of greater power, and sometimes what we are able to do is very limited. But even in times when our hands are tied, **one of the most enormously powerful things we can do is keep the light on**.
Don’t let these people’s bullsh*t get you down. What is so important for us to understand is that as long as we don’t give up, **it’s not over**.
We’re going to keep standing with trans people.
We’re going to keep standing with the LGBTQ+ community.
We’re going to keep standing for the working class.
We’re going to keep fighting for a better minimum wage.
We’re going to keep fighting to guarantee healthcare.
They’re relying on us giving up. **Hell no**.
We will not be afraid – because that’s what they want.
We do not have to comply with illegal activity — **even if that illegal activity is coming from the President of the United States.**
[Help us continue the fight with a grassroots contribution today.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20260114.ztujfk&refcode=em20260114-10582-P_FND_EGR_GRM&t=1&akid=10582%2E2526796%2Esllya9)

In solidarity,
Alexandria

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to become a Founding Donor to our campaign, please use this link to split a contribution today:

Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just _crushing_ Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. _They don’t even believe us._

They're focused on their own wallets — not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices are rising, and our heating bills keep going up. All while the health care and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

Systemic change is the only way to bring down grocery costs, save our fisheries, lower energy prices, and build new housing Alaskans can actually afford.

Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

**This is going to be one of the closest Senate races of the next election, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to win this race... and that is together.**

So I am asking:

[**_Please contribute to my campaign for the U.S. Senate and Maggie Hassan today to become a Founding Donor. clean_body: = Hello — My name is Mary Peltola, and I want to share with you why I've made the decision to run for the United States Senate in Alaska — and to ask for your support as we begin this journey together. But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to become a Founding Donor to our campaign, please use this link to split a contribution today: = | | = Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance. Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity. Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find. So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families. And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. They don’t even believe us. They're focused on their own wallets — not ours. And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest. It’s why our prices are rising, and our heating bills keep going up. All while the health care and services Alaskans rely on get gutted. I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home. Systemic change is the only way to bring down grocery costs, save our fisheries, lower energy prices, and build new housing Alaskans can actually afford. Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again. My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption. Peter -

My name is Mary Peltola, and I want to share with you why I've made the decision to run for the United States Senate in Alaska — and to ask for your support as we begin this journey together.

But if you already understand how important this race and your support are, and you’re ready to become a Founding Donor to our campaign, please use this link to split a contribution today:

CONTRIBUTE [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sm-2601-peltolasplit?amount=]

Now here’s a bit more on how I came to this decision.

When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying 17 bucks for a gallon of milk. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets — not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices are rising, and our heating bills keep going up. All while the health care and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

Systemic change is the only way to bring down grocery costs, save our fisheries, lower energy prices, and build new housing Alaskans can actually afford.

Systemic change is the only way to fill our homes with abundance again.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning.

But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future.

This is going to be one of the closest Senate races of the next election, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to win this race... and that is together.

So I am asking:

Please contribute to my campaign for the U.S. Senate and Seth Magaziner today to become a Founding Donor. We are looking for a huge number of day one donors to get our campaign off to a strong start and put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast.

Mary

This special edition of **AMPED UP** was sober, unsparing, and quietly furious. With Cliff Schecter off for the day, host **David Shuster** led a marathon conversation with **Melissa Corrigan** and **Ellie Leonard** that laid bare how intimidation, violence, and authoritarian logic are no longer creeping into American life--they're operating in the open.
The throughline was unmistakable: _this is what it looks like when power decides the rules no longer apply._
* * *
### 1\. When the FBI Knocks: Journalism Under Direct Threat
The show opened with a jaw-dropping development: FBI agents raiding the home of a Washington Post reporter and seizing her devices after she refused to reveal a source.
Melissa framed the raid for what it is:
**state intimidation of journalists** , enabled by a judge who signed off on it.
Key red flags discussed:
* journalists targeted _after_ sources are already in custody
* devices seized instead of subpoenas litigated in court
* chilling effects on investigative reporting nationwide

Ellie connected the dots to global press repression, warning that this is how democracies slide--_fast_.
* * *
### 2\. "You Have This Thing on Your Phone": Reporting in a Surveillance State
Melissa then pulled the curtain back on the personal cost of real investigative reporting.
She described:
* receiving sensitive federal documents
* realizing her phone had become a liability
* relocating all reporting tools out of her home after repeated drone sightings

This wasn't paranoia--it was professional self-preservation. The message was clear: **journalists are adapting because the government isn 't protecting them.**
* * *
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.ihwfixWVY-xg9-gZLBfviQ9xwz3WwJWwcFmDdotI9cA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=184570311)
* * *
### 3\. Minneapolis: ICE Violence Without Limits
The conversation shifted to Minneapolis, where ICE brutality has escalated since the killing of **Renee Good**.
The panel dissected horrifying footage of:
* an autistic woman violently dragged from her car
* ICE agents screaming contradictory commands
* reporters physically blocked from documenting the scene

Melissa, a Navy veteran, delivered one of the episode's most damning lines:
_" We were prohibited from treating civilians overseas the way ICE is treating Americans now."_
* * *
### 4\. Absolute Immunity Is a Lie--and a Green Light
David zeroed in on the institutional rot:
* DHS officials labeling victims "terrorists"
* J.D. Vance claiming ICE agents have "absolute immunity"
* the FBI withholding evidence from local investigators

That's not chaos. That's **authorization**.
Ellie called it what it is: a system training agents to shoot first, backed by political leaders who will protect them afterward.
* * *
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3722532&post_id=184570311&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTg0NTcwMzExLCJpYXQiOjE3Njg0MzMzNDIsImV4cCI6MTc3MTAyNTM0MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTM3MjI1MzIiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.uRGnP47Ru1ehJssgWD5r0Q6DU7VmJsbhY75DybIZM8o)
* * *
### 5\. White Supremacy Isn't Subtle Anymore
Melissa delivered a devastating assessment:
* ICE didn't exist 25 years ago
* it was born from the Patriot Act's lies
* it now openly signals white supremacist ideology

She described this moment as an **" extinction burst"**--a dying ideology getting louder, crueler, and more violent because it knows it's losing.
* * *
### 6\. Why Independent Journalism Matters--Right Now
The episode closed with a challenge and a charge.
Ellie and Melissa urged viewers to:
* value citizen journalism
* learn how to verify information
* support independent outlets doing the work corporate media won't

David made it explicit: _this kind of reporting survives only if people choose to support it._
Because when intimidation becomes policy, **telling the truth becomes resistance.**

With Cliff Schecter off for the day, host David Shuster led a marathon conversation with Melissa Corrigan and Ellie Leonard that laid bare how intimidation, violence, and authoritarian logic are no longer creeping into American life--they're operating in the open. The throughline was unmistakable: this is what it looks like when power decides the rules no longer apply. 1\. When the FBI Knocks: Journalism Under Direct Threat The show opened with a jaw-dropping development: FBI agents raiding the home of a Washington Post reporter and seizing her devices after she refused to reveal a source. Melissa framed the raid for what it is: state intimidation of journalists , enabled by a judge who signed off on it. Key red flags discussed: journalists targeted after sources are already in custody devices seized instead of subpoenas litigated in court chilling effects on investigative reporting nationwide Ellie connected the dots to global press repression, warning that this is how democracies slide--fast. 2\. "You Have This Thing on Your Phone": Reporting in a Surveillance State Melissa then pulled the curtain back on the personal cost of real investigative reporting. She described: receiving sensitive federal documents realizing her phone had become a liability relocating all reporting tools out of her home after repeated drone sightings This wasn't paranoia--it was professional self-preservation. The message was clear: journalists are adapting because the government isn 't protecting them. 3\. Minneapolis: ICE Violence Without Limits The conversation shifted to Minneapolis, where ICE brutality has escalated since the killing of Renee Good. The panel dissected horrifying footage of: an autistic woman violently dragged from her car ICE agents screaming contradictory commands reporters physically blocked from documenting the scene Melissa, a Navy veteran, delivered one of the episode's most damning lines: " We were prohibited from treating civilians overseas the way ICE is treating Americans now." 4\. Absolute Immunity Is a Lie--and a Green Light David zeroed in on the institutional rot: DHS officials labeling victims "terrorists" J.D. Vance claiming ICE agents have "absolute immunity" the FBI withholding evidence from local investigators That's not chaos. That's authorization. Ellie called it what it is: a system training agents to shoot first, backed by political leaders who will protect them afterward. 5\. White Supremacy Isn't Subtle Anymore Melissa delivered a devastating assessment: ICE didn't exist 25 years ago it was born from the Patriot Act's lies it now openly signals white supremacist ideology She described this moment as an " extinction burst"--a dying ideology getting louder, crueler, and more violent because it knows it's losing. 6\. Why Independent Journalism Matters--Right Now The episode closed with a challenge and a charge. Ellie and Melissa urged viewers to: value citizen journalism learn how to verify information support independent outlets doing the work corporate media won't David made it explicit: this kind of reporting survives only if people choose to support it. Because when intimidation becomes policy, telling the truth becomes resistance. name: Andy Beshear
subject: I believe healthcare is a human right
disclaimer_text: Paid for by In This Together PAC
body:
Healthcare costs are skyrocketing, people are having to choose between buying lifesaving medication or paying rent, and hospitals are losing the critical funding they need to keep their doors open.

Peter,

I believe healthcare is a human right. Every American deserves the ability to see a doctor nearby when they are sick or have a medical emergency. Yet Republicans in Washington are doing everything they can to stop the American people from exercising this right.

Last summer, Republicans voted on a "big, ugly bill" that cut healthcare and will strip millions of Americans of their health insurance. And when Republicans had to choose between extending Affordable Care Act subsidies or closing down the government, they chose the latter with ease.

Now, we're living in a reality where healthcare costs are skyrocketing, people are having to choose between buying lifesaving medication or paying rent, and hospitals are losing the critical funding they need to keep their doors open. **Everyone across the country is feeling the effects of bad GOP policy, but no one is getting hit harder than rural America.**

Here in Kentucky, almost 50% of our population lives in a rural community. I have learned during my time as governor exactly the needs of these communities, and let me tell you: **the local hospital is more than just a healthcare hub.**

In any typical rural community, the local hospital is the second largest employer. They are the driving force behind rural economies – not only do their staff participate in the economy by going to coffee shops, groceries stores, and more, but when they help heal those who are sick, they are helping them get back to work faster or not have to take time off. When our population is healthier, our economy is stronger.

But the Trump administration has become the biggest threat to rural America. Because of the "big, ugly bill," 35 hospitals in Kentucky may close completely or be significantly hurt by underfunding. 200,000 Kentuckians could lose their health insurance. People will have to start driving further away for the care they need, and frankly, it downright angers me to watch politicians in Washington allow this to happen.

This is exactly why we need people-first leaders in our government. We need leaders who will listen to their constituents and stand with them as they make changes in our government that will address the problems they face daily. No American should have to face these rising healthcare costs while their representatives in Congress continue to do nothing.

clean_body: Healthcare costs are skyrocketing, people are having to choose between buying lifesaving medication or paying rent, and hospitals are losing the critical funding they need to keep their doors open. Peter, I believe healthcare is a human right. Every American deserves the ability to see a doctor nearby when they are sick or have a medical emergency. Yet Republicans in Washington are doing everything they can to stop the American people from exercising this right. Last summer, Republicans voted on a "big, ugly bill" that cut healthcare and will strip millions of Americans of their health insurance. And when Republicans had to choose between extending Affordable Care Act subsidies or closing down the government, they chose the latter with ease. Now, we're living in a reality where healthcare costs are skyrocketing, people are having to choose between buying lifesaving medication or paying rent, and hospitals are losing the critical funding they need to keep their doors open. Everyone across the country is feeling the effects of bad GOP policy, but no one is getting hit harder than rural America. Here in Kentucky, almost 50% of our population lives in a rural community. I have learned during my time as governor exactly the needs of these communities, and let me tell you: the local hospital is more than just a healthcare hub. In any typical rural community, the local hospital is the second largest employer. They are the driving force behind rural economies – not only do their staff participate in the economy by going to coffee shops, groceries stores, and more, but when they help heal those who are sick, they are helping them get back to work faster or not have to take time off. When our population is healthier, our economy is stronger. But the Trump administration has become the biggest threat to rural America. Because of the "big, ugly bill," 35 hospitals in Kentucky may close completely or be significantly hurt by underfunding. 200,000 Kentuckians could lose their health insurance. People will have to start driving further away for the care they need, and frankly, it downright angers me to watch politicians in Washington allow this to happen. This is exactly why we need people-first leaders in our government. We need leaders who will listen to their constituents and stand with them as they make changes in our government that will address the problems they face daily. name: Amber Padora
subject: Why hope still matters - even now
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Padora for Colorado
body:
I’m asking as a mom, a wife, and a believer in this movement.

| [|
---](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/SzN38mGpe-bfAxvNjqGFIw~~/AAUS1hA~/dQXwa3x_KrTpl5LofTPtDtmEVF1tBQlJyjvUkYBBeH199lHbvPbNzzeYotl6D4QeVPC7LSlrvP_X93tJ0OYg1PtYuLbnQ8HTXNHSGXT9Zm8ZIG0svL45OOvezOFiJuoW)
| | Friend, I wanted to check in with you personally as a mom, a wife, and someone who believes deeply in this movement. **Like many families right now, we are having hard conversations at home.**
Our kids are asking questions no child should have to ask. Why people are being taken away? Why there are protests? Why so much feels scary? We try to be honest without frightening them. And when things feel overwhelming, John always reminds them of something Mr. Rogers taught us.
**When you see scary things happening, look for the helpers.** That is what we have been trying to do.
**And it is what gives me hope.** Over the holidays, we were able to step away briefly from work and campaigning and spend time together exploring Colorado. We absolutely loved it. The open spaces and quiet time together reminded us why we love this state so deeply and why it is worth fighting for. **>From our family to yours, we hope you had a wonderful holiday.** I will not pretend these are easy times. Families are hurting. Children are scared. ICE is being used in ways that terrify communities, not protect them. Many parents are struggling to reassure their kids that things will be okay. But this weekend, John and I stood with hundreds of neighbors at anti ICE protests, and once again, **we saw the helpers.** Compassion. Courage. People refusing to turn away from one another. **I believe this with everything in me. The good will always outweigh the bad in the end.** Our community in Colorado and across this country is full of empathetic, decent people. Even those who have lost their way are not our enemies. They are neighbors who have been misled or hurt. Because we love this country and this state, we are willing to fight to help steer us back on course. John asked me to share a campaign update, so here it is from the heart. **John is hitting the ground running.** Protests. Community roundtables. Long drives across the Eastern Plains. Town halls in Aurora and Lone Tree. Every conversation he has reinforces the same truth. **People are ready for change.** He is working his day job during the day and building this campaign late into the night because he believes this fight is worth it for our kids and for yours. What he will not tell you, but I will, is this.
**We are behind this month.** So many of you have already given what you can, even as costs keep rising. Some of you wish you could give more than five dollars. Please know this. **Every single contribution matters. Every single one.** John is refusing corporate PAC money and mega donor funding. Instead, he is choosing something harder. **A campaign powered by people who believe our democracy and our children’s future are worth fighting for.** As a mother and John’s partner in this campaign, not just to defeat Lauren Boebert but to uplift working people and defend democracy, **I need to ask for your help.** If we do not pick up fundraising this month, we will have to slow down right as caucus, assembly, and forums ramp up. So I am asking you today with gratitude and hope. [**Can you help us keep this movement going?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/BOHVQ0rLKKdOuOjCq9CNZA~~/AAUS1hA~/7Kjc5P72vxpxn6ZpScnSaj6yfjZhz8eiwo5A09SfHBwsnjz0l0K9D-h9w1IxRiOdpHIZW2RRvjm0VI-c4Bj3NEh_Bg1rz8W0XCNOdGJ52L01YDkCsyxZxXllh6Z_fxXY6glAUTagY05p4gqTwvoMt6E7Uqy4-MjOO3Vxa0dFYyg~) Whatever you are able to give helps John keep showing up, keep fighting, and keep reminding our children that helpers still exist and that loving this country means refusing to give up on it. **Thank you for standing with us.** With love and determination,
**Amber Padora** _**P.S. Even five dollars helps keep the lights on, the car on the road, and this movement moving forward. We are deeply grateful for you.**_ _****_**[In dark times, love for our kids and our country is what keeps us fighting.](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/BOHVQ0rLKKdOuOjCq9CNZA~~/AAUS1hA~/7Kjc5P72vxpxn6ZpScnSaj6yfjZhz8eiwo5A09SfHBwsnjz0l0K9D-h9w1IxRiOdpHIZW2RRvjm0VI-c4Bj3NEh_Bg1rz8W0XCNOdGJ52L01YDkCsyxZxXllh6Z_fxXY6glAUTagY05p4gqTwvoMt6E7Uqy4-MjOO3Vxa0dFYyg~)** If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | [Chip in $10 now >>](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/syGQ-L26KudRRQmDgNPsiQ~~/AAUS1hA~/qSLH3DzG8JTZBYJbK5ycsqIJhYpeY38T9nkMYFKeR3VKROWrWivSgSDey4ngJ7bnbahwqYm-mRgsNCK0jUyxnuwVULtQc3JHJtJ0m7uXWzoTgquU_HcbN6KOTxq2MgziK_HdJPeMm_KzS20ncFZ8RwG0Vz6HbYBEMBdTp8U_z7rg7w4DuXFj3_F0vIuWH4_U) | [Chip in $25 now >>](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/aZ8EFHgOMKxvdCGcOopm6w~~/AAUS1hA~/qSLH3DzG8JTZBYJbK5ycsqIJhYpeY38T9nkMYFKeR3VKROWrWivSgSDey4ngJ7bnbahwqYm-mRgsNCK0jUyxnuwVULtQc3JHJtJ0m7uXWzp8_3VhTA-5DlROwYzyoFnHoKINkxhPEmgmdbWvk8kbSCFnPjq9RpQqTahuJuBI1-aH0i9__23Ky9vnf2Iht_DM)

name: Oregon Department of Justice
subject: Update from AG Dan Rayfield: Strategic Vision & Upcoming Town Halls
body:
Strategic Vision; Town Halls on Jan 21 & Jan 30
---
| | | |
---
|
# Today, we're announcing our 2026 Strategic Vision for Oregon DOJ.
When I was sworn in as AG on December 31, 2024, I said that the significance of this responsibility could not come at a more meaningful time in our state’s and our nation's history. As we enter the second year of this administration, the challenges facing Oregonians demand even more from us. Thankfully, after a year of getting to know the incredible people who keep the Oregon Department of Justice running every day, I've never been more confident in our ability to meet this moment. Read on for:
* Our 2026 Strategic Vision
* Federal Oversight & Accountability Town Hall with 5 AGs on Jan. 21
* Oregon Priorities Town Hall in Forest Grove on Jan. 30
* and more!

In service, Dan Rayfield, Oregon Attorney General
---
| |
* * *
---
|
# 2026 Strategic Vision
Today, **we released our[2026 Strategic Vision](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.doj.state.or.us%2Fwp-content%2Fuploads%2F2026%2F01%2FStrategic-Vision.pdf/1/0101019bbee68f38-ef2c46bc-786b-418c-82e5-22794ad7c99e-000000/-iwWXfCr4r55lcrbWRLZU-LThOn1D52rUYCS04H0c2U=440),** focused on keeping communities safe, fighting for consumers, seniors, and working families, upholding our shared values, and strengthening the foundation of the agency for generations to come. It is both ambitious and grounded in the reality that we must be more efficient, more strategic, and more focused than ever before. [Read the 2026 Strategic Vision.](https://links-2.govdelivery.com/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.doj.state.or.us%2Foregon-department-of-justice%2Foffice-of-the-attorney-general%2F2026-strategic-vision%2F/1/0101019bbee68f38-ef2c46bc-786b-418c-82e5-22794ad7c99e-000000/1zhJyyf9wP-sU-bAmQoRPjnA_rH97pzDD_-7fUOpE3s=440)

# Federal Oversight & Accountability Town Hall on Jan. 21
Next Wednesday, January 21, we’re hosting a **Federal Oversight & Accountability Town Hall with four visiting state AGs at Revolution Hall in Portland. **

**[It's RMD Time Again.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e24452762/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsMURvaGFRMQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWgsag/sfp5ebad2cb)** **Imagine opening your retirement statement this year...** And realizing that a simple decision - one most retirees never even think about - could reshape your taxes, your diversification, and even your long-term financial stability. Every year, Americans over age 73 are forced to withdraw **tens of billions of dollars** from their retirement accounts. And year after year, most people follow the same path: **Take the RMD in cash and move on.** Not because it's the best choice. But because no one ever tells them there's another way. **[The "Default" RMD Isn't Your Only Option.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e24452762/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsMURvaGFRMQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWgsag/sfp5ebad2cb)** Financial institutions make it easy to withdraw cash. Too easy. But simple isn't always strategic. Taking your RMD in cash may:
* Increase taxable income
* Force you to sell assets at moments that may not
align with your plan
* Reduce the overall portion of your wealth that remains invested

And yet... **[There's an IRS-Approved Alternative Most Retirees Never Hear About.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e24452762/VaHR0cHM6Ly9scC5hbGxlZ2lhbmNlZ29sZC5jb20vcm1kLWRlZC1iLw/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjAxMTQ/LbmNsMURvaGFRMQ/qP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9QW1lcmljYUZpcnN0V2FyUm9vbSZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPURjdGQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPUFtZXJpY2FGaXJzdFdhclJvb20xLTE0/gaWgsag/sfp5ebad2cb)** Few realize that **RMDs can also be taken "in-kind."** Meaning: instead of withdrawing cash, you can receive _certain assets directly_ without liquidating them first. No, it doesn't eliminate taxes. But for many savers, it may help them:
* Preserve their long-term allocation
* Avoid being forced to sell during volatile markets
* Strengthen diversification, depending on their strategy

It's fully IRS-allowed... but rarely mentioned in traditional planning conversations. **Before You Take Your Next RMD, Ask Yourself:**
* Do I know _most_ IRS-approved ways to satisfy my distribution?
